recensioni.testo: Excellent school, all the teachers I met were extremely nice and helpful. You are motivated to get out of your comfort zone and really start speaking Italian. The focus is on real, daily conversations.

Best school of Italian language! I studied there 11 years back and had a really good time there learning and making new friends while exploring the beautiful city of Firenze. I totally recommend this school

Highly qualified teachers, and a very friendly atmosphere. Meeting people from all over the world is an amazing experience; everyone is always willing to help you out and you get to learn a lot about each other's cultures.
Plus, the location is great (lots of nice places nearby with great food)

Phenomenal experience at Linguviva Firenze! The teachers were incredible, made the students feel very comfortable. Different levels of classes are available so even if you are brand new to a second language or more experienced they will take care of you. Meeting other students from all over the world, my class consisted of Americans, South Americans, Europeans, Asians and various age groups -- I was 28 when i attended and had ages above and below me which was a nice mix. And the city itself needs no explanation, just gorgeous! I've attended twice, so would highly recommend :)

A very very good language school! Very welcoming atmosphere, you are treated like a guest not like "just another student"(which is not normal for the brache). The teaching methods are to me very close to recent science and therefore better than in most language schools: They teach the grammar & the writing very well, but set the focus from the beginning on practicing talking and hearing. Therefore you gain the feeling for the language in unnormal speed. This meets with the expiriences of my peers. One said: I have never ever studied somewhere as good as here.
Highly recommendable

I had the most amazing 3 weeks studying Italian at Scuola Leonardo da Vinci. I started off in A1 (Elementare 2), and left at A2 (Elementare 3). I originally enrolled for only 2 weeks, but added a 3rd because I loved it so much. The enrolment process was very smooth, and the staff were so helpful and friendly throughout the whole experience. I am currently working towards moving to Italy, and this was the best thing I have ever done for myself. Learning at the school and living in Firenze. Best decision ever.

I especially want to give praise to my teachers, Marco and Camilla. Their knowledge was evident right from the start, and I could tell they genuinely care about their students and their success. They also were so patient with me, and corrected my mistakes gently, which is something I really appreciate. They also made learning Italian fun. I also liked it was all in Italian, even from day 1 and you’re thrown head first into the language. I learned so much from both of them. Grazie mille! 🤗

I will be continuing my studies online, and will return to the school in person as soon as I can. I highly recommend studying Italian at Scuola Leonardo da Vinci in Firenze!

I stayed at scuola LDV in Florence for one week, at B1 level and it was a great experience. The teachers are wonderful, I did not only learn the language but also a lot about the Italian culture and habits. It was great meeting students from across the globe and from all ages, also after school you don’t need to worry about getting bored ;).
One week was definitely too short so I will be back!

If you want to learn Italian and experience the culture alongside other learners then Scuola Leonardo is a great choice.  Our teacher, Francesca, was great.  I appreciated her enunciation.  We were able to speak Italian (I’m just a little past basic beginner stage so I needed that) and it felt truly intensive.  Be prepared to be in class for half a day with homework assignments.  They have fun but take it seriously!  You will need to take a test at the end of your course to determine your level of fluency.  Don’t worry about it unless you have to learn Italian and then I’d say make sure you study and practice each day.  Now that I’ve returned home, I’ll continue online through Scuola Leonardo.  Then, I’ll be going back in person for a longer stay.  It’s been the best decision.  I’d highly encourage the combination of online and in person if you really want to learn Italian proficiently without stressing yourself out too much.

I attended Scuola Leonardo da Vinci for 2 weeks as an A1 student, while my husband and son started out as beginners. For me it was a refresher after learning Italian many years ago and forgetting much of it in the intervening years. I felt very challenged to begin with, but with teacher Antonella’s help and a strong focus in classes on speaking Italian all the time, I steadily regathered some of my skills and confidence. The school is not only well organised and provides excellent teachers, but also arranges fun and educational activities to help develop language skills and cultural understanding. I would happily go back again!

I am 76 and attended the course for two weeks as a B1 student. It was a wonderful and challenging experience. Our main teacher showed immense patience with a diverse group. At times her Italian was rather rapid but the immersive nature of the course meant one tuned in. There were numerous opportunities to speak and Maria Grazia was excellent at encouraging dialogue. Some of the group were very fluent. The concentration was on grammar which I always find hard but repetition is the key. The organisation was superb from initial booking to accommodation. My own accommodation was excellent and a mere 10 minutes from the centrally placed school. The older students had the La Dolce Vita programme in the afternoons. This was wonderfully organised by Antonella who was the perfect guide. She escorted us to a variety of venues and covered a multitude of subjects relevant to Florence. Her voice was always clear and she spoke slowly enough for us to follow and understand every word. She provided the icing on an already rich cake!
I wholeheartedly recommend the course for the clarity of the teaching, the camaraderie with fellow students and the extracurricular afternoons.

I have just completed one month at ABC School in Florence, and my experience has been truly enriching. I began my journey here as a beginner in Italian, and I can already see significant progress in my understanding of the language.

I would like to sincerely appreciate the leadership of Brenda and Beatrice for their warm, polite, and welcoming approach. Their dedication creates a positive and supportive learning environment for all students.

My heartfelt thanks also go to my teachers—Greta, Serena, Noemi, and Maya—who have been exceptionally kind, patient, and accommodating. Their respectful and encouraging attitude made learning both comfortable and enjoyable.

What stands out most is the quality of teaching. The lessons are logically structured and thoughtfully designed, helping students not only learn the language but also explore Italian culture. The integration of grammar and conversation sessions is very effective, making the learning process both practical and engaging.

Overall, ABC School offers a well-organized and enriching learning experience. I highly recommend it to anyone who wishes to learn Italian in a supportive and professional environment.

I recommend ABC scuola with all my heart. I just finished one week italian course and I wish I could stay longer. Everyone from the staff have had very kind and welcoming approach- starting with Monica with whom contact during registration was always easy and super helpful, through the staff of the school and the teachers- Greta and Naomi, very kind and patient teachers which made learning effective but also fun.  The program after the classes was various and inspiring to learn more about the culture and history of Florence. Grazie mille! I hope to come back one day!🫶

The experience of a lifetime!

I cannot praise ABC School highly enough.  From start to finish, my 3-weeks there was amazing.  First, the school director, Monica, is highly responsive to all your inquiries, and works diligently to craft exactly the program you want to have.  Once you arrive, the school secretary, Conny, is equally helpful, making excursion suggestions and telephone reservations on your behalf, and well as just generally making sure that you are happy about every aspect of your ABC School experience.  The language instructors are amazing teachers, and really work hard to make the classes enjoyable.  They also go the extra mile, and craft additional exercises outside the standard book curriculum when they see you have a weakness in a particular area (oh, you evil pronouns), plus move you around as needed to make sure you are always with students of a similar level.
ABC also organizes student group activities after classes.  While I was there, we did a guided walk up to San Miniato al Monte, a cooking class, museum visits to the Accademia and the Uffizi, and popular evenings out for appericena and pizza.  On Saturdays, teachers also escort interested students to neighboring towns such as Pisa, Siena and Lucca.

In addition to the morning Italian-language classes, I also took a course in Art History.  Once again, Monica works with you to make sure you study exactly the artist(s) and/or time period that interests you the most.  During the course, you have a private, 1 on 1 class with an Art History teacher.  Each day you have a lecture or visit 1 or 2 locations throughout Florence with just your own art history specialist.  The teacher makes sure that the class is tailored to what you are most interested in… more history?  More art techniques? Just let them know.  They are also excellent about suggesting other places to visit on your own that you might be interested in (because of funding restrictions, many museums have very strange hours – one place was open only Mon-Thurs, from 3-5 p.m.)   In short, you are given a private, guided tour through one world’s richest art cities.  Even if I forget 50% of what I learned, I’ll still be roughly 4,000 times smarter than before I took ABC’s art history course!

I can’t think of a better place to learn and study Italian.  I’d recommend ABC School to everyone.

I have studied at a few different language schools in different countries and I can definitely say that the ABC School in Florence is my favourite. Most importantly, the teachers and teaching style is very effective. You are encouraged to speak Italian immediately and the teachers are so incredibly friendly that it is never intimidating!  You have really small classes as well (maximum 8 people) so you really do get a personal, intense learning experience and after a few weeks you will definitely feel like your Italian has improved.

What I also like about the school is that they organise accommodation for you as well as afternoon activities (food tours, films, museums, culture seminars etc.) so you're never bored and there is always the opportunity to improve your Italian even more in the afternoon. Lastly the school is in a great location. It's right in the historic centre in the Santa Croce quarter in the beautiful Florence which means that all the museums and restaurants are right at your doorstep. Definitely come here if you're interested in learning or improving your Italian, you won't regret it!

I studied at ABC for 3 weeks in the summers of 2014 and 2015.  The teachers are amazing and I highly recommend the school.  I liked that the students are of various ages and come from many different countries.  The course book is unique to the school.  I also think the location is very convenient and allows you to immerse yourself in day to day Florence life.

The real Florentine restaurant you can’t miss.
Back in Florence after very long time, I literally stumbled into this fabulous place. Very well managed and highly focused on the quality of the ingredients.
It really is the cozy little restaurant we were looking for.

Did you ever want to find that little neighborhood gem of a restaurant run by nonna and nonno with the most fresh and authentic Tuscan food you can imagine? This is the place. We sampled almost everything on the menu and it was an amazing collection of flavors.

We were immediately welcomed by who we assumed to be the owners of the restaurant. They were so kind and welcoming and you could see how much pride they took in their business and their food. The food was delicious and was such a great value for what we paid, I couldn't believe our luck stumbling into this little place. Thank you for being the highlight of our trip!
Can only recommend to visit this lovely family driven restaurant. Both food and the owners was an absolute delight. Will for sure be back at this treasure
Some of the best meals we've had in italy 🇮🇹, felt like home 🏠 cooking, delicious 😋

I enrolled in the Senior 50+ program and it was wonderful! The teachers were excellent-- knowledgeable, patient, very kind and friendly. The extra-curricular activities (cooking classes, museum tours, excursions, group dinners and concerts) were very well-organized and highly enjoyable. The staff went above and beyond to ensure that the students  (a very diverse mix from all over the world) could not only improve their language skills but also appreciate the rich tapestry of Italian history, culture and daily life. To all of them I say "bravissimi tutti e grazie mille!"

I had an amazing experience at the school. The classes and the professors are amazing. I was able to take italian classes, cooking classes, and painting for the time I was in Florence. The school also organizes activities such as wine tasting, pizza tasting, day trips, etc. to learn more about the Italian culture and practice the language.

I spent two weeks at the beginning of this year taking an intensive Italian course, and I absolutely enjoyed my time there! The institute is excellent, with professional teachers who not only help you grasp the language but also understand Italian culture. We were grouped based on our level into smaller classes, which helped for more communication and practice in speaking. All materials were provided, making it very convenient. Additionally, there are study books available that you can buy to continue learning on your own after the course is over.
The institute organized activities both during the week and on weekends - we got to see Siena and thanks to our lovely guide we understood more about the history of the city.
The institute is truly authentic, situated in a great location, and provided me with the opportunity to make new friends from around the world. I would love to return someday to further enhance my language skills!

Thank you Domenico and the whole team for having me and always being very helpful.

Absolutely LOVED spending 3 weeks with this institute! The best teachers, staff, and community!! I really believe in this incredible place and think it’s one of the best. I was becoming so present and strong with the language.

Each lesson is structured as a grammar lesson in the morning and then a conversational focused lesson in the afternoon.

They also do class trips on the weekends to neighboring cities. (Pictured below is Lucca)

If you have a long stay or even want to try out a week, I highly recommend this place!

Best language school in Florence. What a wonderful experience! This authentic Italian language and arts school has been around for almost 50 years and is still run « family style » even though they have up to 150 students at a time during peak season. With highly competent teachers in all levels of Italian (A1 to C2 levels), small classes of maximum 10 students, and many cultural activities (weekend trips as well as excellent guided tours of Florence highlights such as Santa Maria Novella church and Palazzo Vecchio every week), you will make friends of all ages and cultures (students range from 17 years old to 75!) and learn Italian at your own pace. They also offer cooking classes, art classes, and private lessons, which are all very much appreciated by the students. A shoutout to Claudio, who teaches with passion and precision, and helped me improve tremendously in 4 weeks. Grazie mille!!

I studied at Europass from May 2025 to February 2026, and it was truly a life-changing experience.
Having studied with almost all the teachers—from Martina to Bianca, Domenica, and Donatella—I can say they are all exceptional. They built my Italian language foundation so perfectly that I reached a C1 level, despite my native language being Arabic. Their lessons were always engaging, enriching, and fun.
Even though I was in Florence on my own, I never felt lonely. This school is so welcoming that it felt like being with family.
A special thanks to the wonderful Francesca for making my journey so beautiful and comfortable. I highly recommend this school to everyone 🌟

Grazie di cuore per tutto!

Europass in Florence is an amazing school if you are looking to learn Italian. I initially did a one week intensive course with Maurizio as my professor and Estefania as my one on one intensive lesson professor and it was amazing. As a flight attendant I needed to learn Italian quickly and thanks to their dedication, knowledge, kindness and preparedness I was able to pass my Italian test for work. My experience was so pleasant that I decided to come back for another week yet this time for personal growth. The school, the staff and the activities they organize after class are top notch. I can’t recommend the school (especially Maurizio and Estefania) enough; they truly are beyond amazing!

I had a really nice time in Firenze during my language holiday. The lessons in the morning had a warm and friendly atmosphere, we learned a lot about the language and Italy from our teacher, Donatella. The sighseeings guided by teachers gave us a lot more than any tourist guide book, and we could listen it in Italian! I can highly recommend the course to anybody who wants to improve their Italian and have a nice time in Toscana!

Wonderful experience with Europass!! I learnt a lot in the 2 week intensive course and the cultural visits with Maurizio in the afternoon were top!!! Everyone was super friendly and willing to help, teachers and the team at the office organizing everything!
I would definitely recommend Europass to whoever is willing to learn Italian in Florence!

It was a fantastic expirience, dream come true! Beautiful Florence and of course a beautiful language, that I could enjoy not only by listening but also by pronouncing the melodious words. I'm greatful to the staff of Europass that made this possible.
Studying in an old beautiful building, which is steeped with history, the atmosphere at school is light and easy, the quality of teaching is just excellent. I was really able to send and receive messages after 5 day of classes. Special thanks to Elena!
Really, unforgettable experience!
I had it combined with cooking classis by the way and it was fun!

great scuola with nice teachers and a very friendly team. They care a lot to help you and make you feel comfortable. You also meet a lot of very interesting people from all over the world coming here to learn Italian!

I recommend to take care of a room in time and not to late. My first room was actually bad so I had to move into a new room after one week. However the Team was very supportive to get me another room asap!

Great school ! Did a 6 month course there with many different teachers, all super professional, patient and kind. Small classes, interesting topics and lessons. Amazing after school activities that introduce you to the history of Florence and the Italian culture. Great team of secretaries, patient helpful and flexible with the students' needs. Very highly recommended! Would definitely return as soon as I get a chance :))

I can’t recommend Centro Machiavelli enough! Mario and the team were wonderful to deal with and super helpful in organising not only my Italian language classes but finding me an opportunity to work in Florence! The best part was the activities outside class time that involved other students at the school, helping me make life-long friends from all over the world as well as improving my Italian! I will never forget my time in Florence, Grazie Mille ❤️

Machiavelli school in Florence is the best foreign language school that I have frequented in Italy. Professional, friendly and very accommodating in all aspects. The instructors are top notch and make a great effort in teaching Italian— as could be appreciated by a resident living and growing up in Italy.

I feel really happy to have made this choice. Quite professional, organized. The staff is really well-educated not just in Italian as a language but also in history, cooking, painting, yoga and many more.

I thank my teachers, Brenda, Silvia y Vincenza, for all the things that I learned. You girls made this experience amazing and I hope, I will see you again to show you my progress and share some laughs.

Highly recommended.

Fantastic experience. Im from Uruguay and signed up for 2 full day workshops on acrylics and watercolours and received the most dedicated instruction and recommendations. Tommy, the multilingual maestro, guides you expertly, patiently, and without criticism.  I strongly recommend Accademia del Giglio to any serious and dedicated artist who wants to improve and expand on their skills. Thank you Tommy and team!

One of the best experiences I ever had. I was fortunate to have a two day class with this amazing group of instructors. Though I haven’t painted in over a couple years, from the way they guided me, everything came back naturally. Highly recommend.

PS
Initially they helped me schedule my class accordingly with my travel plans. That was a huge plus too

Fantastico! I learned so much this week at Accademia del Giglio. I did the half-day, week-long program and I am a beginner artist (focusing on drawing). I was in a room with about 4 other students and we all were able to learn what we wanted. Stefano, our amazing teacher, worked 1-to-1 with each of us and really managed the class well, balancing instruction (in English or Italian) with exercises/practice. I left with so much confidence and enthusiasm.

The school is in a great location and I believe it's perfect for any age/skill/ability. Highly recommend - in fact, I'm planing to return again!

My sisters and I had a great time at Rosy’s class. Watercolouring along the Arno helped us to decompress after long days of sight seeing. Rosy was able to accommodate multiple levels of experience, and we all had a good time. We even bought our own watercolour set at a local art store and have continued to paint as we travel through Italy.

Such an excellent experience!  I'm from Canada, and I recently completed a three-month curriculum at Accademia del Giglio.  The open structure helps you focus on what you want to learn, and I can't say enough good things about the staff - always attentive and polite, making every day enjoyable.  The instructors are very patient and give great feedback during the creative process.  I'm a painter with a lot of experience and although I usually paint alone, it was so nice to paint alongside others every day - discussing art creation and life as an artist. I attended from November through January and I'd highly recommend this time of year (quiet time for tourism and beautiful holiday displays!).  Special thanks to Lorenzo for helping me finally get to the school! - Molto Grazie!

I chose Scuola Toscana for a week-long Italian course, mainly because they offer private classes, which I had been looking for—and it exceeded my expectations. I truly feel I maximized my learning in that one week. The teachers are very knowledgeable and professional, yet approachable and kind. They offer a variety of programs (family stays, cultural experiences, etc.), and still manage to blend students together seamlessly across programs. I also really enjoyed the extracurricular activities in the afternoons. Overall, a very pleasant and productive experience. I will definitely come back.

It was the second time that we traveled to Italy and started the vacation with language lessons. La Scuola Toscana is a great school. The two of us are at different language levels, and therefore we had a total of six teachers, who were all remarkably competent, patient, interesting, and kind.

The school is also very well located in the historic center of Florence. The classrooms are spacious and comfortable, and the optional school-sponsored activities are interesting.  We recommend this school highly.

This is an amazing school. We did the  beginner Italian family course for one week but would have gladly stayed much longer. Our kids ages 4 and 9 years old thoroughly enjoyed it. The teachers are top notch. Vibrant, animated and immerse you totally into an Italian world of a great learning adventure. Class size was small and therefore very personal.
The afternoon excursions are very informative and nicely arranged.
A Wonderful !!wonderful school !!

I've been to this school multiple times now because not only is it really helpful and educational, it's really fun, and you get to be in Florence, which is an amazing city. The school is great. The instructors are all brilliant at what they do and are fun to be around. Plus they cater the classes to your skill level regardless whether you're a beginner or an advanced student.

Besides the classes, they offer after school and weekend events/activities, which are always fun, entertaining and educational. Sometimes you'll go to other cities, or take you to eat at the hot spots that only the locals know about, or you can take cooking lessons, or historical tours of Florence, which are beyond fascinating. I've done many amazingly fun things with the school.

I had such a great time at Scuola Toscana! The staff were very friendly and supportive. There were a lot of different fun activities for students to take part in. I can't imagine a more perfect place to study than Florence. A truly great experience!

Highly recommend Istituto Il David! The school's organization is outstanding, and the homestay arrangement was perfect. The teachers are fantastic, making the classes engaging with a great mix of grammar and real-world conversation. Plus, there was a wonderful, diverse mix of students in the group, which made learning even more enjoyable. The location is very central, perfect for exploring Florence after class. Thanks to the whole team for a memorable week!

Well-organised classes! Excellent teachers! There are also additional activities, particularly city tours! And, most of all, the person responsible for the smooth work of the school is Maria, the secretary. Her human touch and quick reactions are the reason why I've chosen this school!  I hope to come back to the school in the near future! Vlasta Peric

This school is excellent. I’ve attended language courses at other schools before, and this one is truly the best.

The teachers are fantastic — Giada, I miss our grammar and conversation classes so much! The extracurricular activities are also very interesting (the walk around Florence with Anna was fascinating — even the rain didn’t bother us).

The organization is very good, and everything runs on time. Most importantly, everyone at the school — Maria from the school office, the management, and all the teachers — is incredibly helpful, professional, and kind.

Communication with the office before the course was also very important to me. I received answers to all my questions, and all the documents were prepared exactly as needed.

The location is another big advantage — right in the city center, with plenty of lunch options nearby and lots of attractions to explore after classes.

I sincerely recommend this school and hope I will have the opportunity to study here again.

I studied Italian at Istituto il David for 2 weeks and had a really great experience. The teachers were excellent and the activities after school were also really fun. I felt like their materials were some of the best I’ve seen, and I advanced my ability to speak Italian more than at other schools I have attended. I still have a long way to go though!

I wasn’t going to leave a review after my experience 4 years ago, but after seeing a few other comments with similar experiences, I feel it’s necessary to. I started at what should have been an A0 level. All the students in my class had at least a high A1 level if not more. Not only was the pace too fast, but if I got flustered and didn’t know an answer, instead of skipping to another student, the teacher would just stare at me and it was humiliating. After 2 weeks, I had extreme panic attacks and had to drop out. I ended up getting a private tutoring for a bit. I told her when I was getting stuck and didn’t understand what we were studying or she was going too fast. I don’t know if she was impatient with the pace or if the school was pressuring her, but her whole demeanor changed and I decided it wasn’t a good fit. I truly believe they need a better system so true beginners are able to find a class that is encouraging and a good fit. The school may be fine for students that want to increase their knowledge and have an intensive lesson course, but not good at all for beginners.

I studied at Parola Italian Language School for one month, preparing for the B2 CILS exam. The groups were rather small, and the teachers could focus on every student, which optimized the learning experience. What helped me most were the private lessons with Sara, fully adapted to my personal learning goals and difficulties. Grazie mille

When I moved to Italy from Denmark in 2023, I came all alone and didn’t know anyone. Scuola Parola became very important for me, it was my security and safety. I went to group classes, but mostly individual classes. The school was another family and they helped me with my Italian, but also with a lot of other stuff. Housing, doctors, restaurants etc. Being new in Florence all by yourself can be difficult in the beginning, so having a place where you feel safe and a place that feels like family is essential. I also went back in 2025 to my usual teacher at parola and had some classes, and it was so fun to be back. Now I have been in Florence for 3 years and would always recommend Parola to newcomers. I will always be thankful for the impact the school and the teachers had on my wellbeing in Florence

The best of Florence! Parola language school was my best experience of 6 months in beautiful Florence. The very friendly, charming and highly professional staff made me feel welcome and relaxed. Classes were fun and challenging with an inspiring range of people of all age groups and nationalities. At Parola I not only learned to speak Italian but also obtained a deeper insight into the Italian culture and particularities. I enjoyed the different  outings and guided tours. Thank you so much for this great enrichment!

Such an amazing school!! Both times that I have been here, I have had a wonderful time! The staff is so helpful and kind and the teachers are very funny and truly make you enjoy the lessons! Everybody here makes you feel at home despite the fact that you are actually in another country! I am so grateful for my experience and cannot wait to come back to Scuola Parola a third time!! Grazie mille!!!

I am extremely happy I chose to study at Parola. Originally when I was looking for a language school to study at in Italy, Parola was one of the first schools to show up on my search. After deciding to choose to study here, Gianluca made my enrollment process very easy as he was very communicative and helpful. I enrolled myself as a beginner into the “Allegro” intensive group course, as well as taking private lessons. My first day at Parola was a little overwhelming as the teachers immediately began to teach in Italian, but after a week I noticed myself comprehending the language at a faster pace and my vocabulary slowly improving. The teachers at Parola are some of the friendliest and most patient people I have met, which made the learning experience more enjoyable and kept me motivated when the lessons felt difficult. Parola organizes plenty of extra curricular activities, such as touring the streets of Florence or my favorite: an Italian hand gestures class. I met so many people from all around the world as we bonded over interest in the Italian language, not only did I get to learn about Italian culture but also the cultures of my classmates. My seven weeks at Parola were some of my best moments, and I wouldn’t have changed this experience for anything else. Grazie mille allo staff di Parola per avermi regalato un’esperienza così incredibile!
It's a fantastic center for learning Italian. The teachers are excellent, all native speakers, and they make the classes really enjoyable. Highly recommended.
Entertaining, dynamic, and highly educational classes. Exceptional teacher.

The best Italian school in all of Madrid.
Small classes and wonderful teachers.

recensioni.autore: Oscar Luis Martin Vazquez (Gerente / Jefe de SAT)
recensioni.testo: A great place to learn Italian, the teacher is lovely and of course a very good teacher. I couldn't finish due to work reasons, but if I have to enroll again, it will be here.
I took the B1 course this year and I couldn't be happier. Small groups, excellent and friendly teachers. They also offer free tutoring on basic topics. I highly recommend it!
Great school,lovely location and a great staff!
It is a flexible school.  Family atmosphere.  Excellent programs: Music,  Italian,  internhips...

Disappointing experience.
The housing recommended by Academia Europea Di Firenze was in poor condition, and the owner, Cristiana Amendola, treated students in an unprofessional manner. The Academia was not aware of the situation until I provided photos and another student reported similar issues.

I had to stop my studies early because of this. The owner refunded only one week out of the full month paid in advance, and the school did not offer any refund for the unused portion of my studies.

I recommend being very careful with housing suggestions and any arrangements made outside of the school.

First, the location of the Academy is prefect, easily accessible from multiple points of the city. The instructors are engaging and committed, and the admin staff are extremely welcoming and offer helpful tips for your stay. While I'm still in the early days of my Italian course, I found the academy to be a great second home away from home and have already met some great students of all ages and backgrounds. They really do try to foster a safe community!

Such an great place to learn and meet new people. It has been such an amazing experience to be here and study here. All after school activities are so amusing and helpful for creating a community. I've lover my time here!
Marvelous experience that i never wish to finish! Love the people, love the classes and absolutely love the school. A ginormous Thank you for all the accademia

The Accademia Europea di Firenze is the perfect place to dive into Italian culture. The teachers are amazing—knowledgeable, passionate, and always supportive.

The classes are fun and engaging, and the atmosphere is very welcoming.

It’s a wonderful way to learn and experience the beauty of Florence.

Highly recommended!

Absolute rip off the interior design summer course! Don’t go there as the only thing you get out of this place is sitting in a classroom and working independently on an interior design project, without any assistance or good help from the teacher, who doesn’t even speak English.

I literally paid 2,7k for only sitting in a room without AC and practicing my own skills I already got from other schools.

Sorry but you don’t learn anything new here and you will be highly disappointed for booking a course with them.

Also on the first day, before the orientation started, I went to the bathroom for 2 minutes and wanted to go the classroom for the orientation but they asked me to wait outside because I was late. Eventhough the teacher shows me where the bathroom is😂

Such a joke! So I missed the orientation and waited like a bad child in front of the classroom.

Don’t support this school and sign up for the FIDI summer course which at least is 1 month long and half the price + you get much more knowledge out of it.

Cannot recommend this school!

I was a student at Accademia Riaci this winter and took an Art History Course. There isn't enough words to describe my experience fully! It won't be an exaggeration to say it was one of the best experiences of my life. The information given, the places visited with the group, the discussions held – everything was amazing and gave a new perspective on art I've always loved and admired. Moreover, studying helped to make new friends and find new interests, so I can only dream of going back to Firenze and learning more:)
Thank you for everything!! I already miss the lessons and walks we had during the course

I am a person that had always wanted to travel and study abroad, but I am also the person that was so homesick I couldn't eat for 3 days after going to college. So making the final decision to go to Italy was scary for me but one of the best ones I had ever made.
I completely fell in love with everything about Accademia Riaci and the shoemaking program, and of course I fell in love with Florence. The assistants and the teacher, Mr. Angelo, were so helpful and very patient to teach me all the steps to create my first pair of handmade shoes. Looking forward to coming back next summer!!!

I've just finished my leather bag making course for 3 months and it was a very enriching experience. I wanna thank the teacher Giuliana for her amazing support. Also the school staff was very friendly and helpful with everyone.

Amazing experience. Headed to Florence in a small school studying interior design, I was initially nervous. However, within the first week, the school staff and the teacher helped me to feel like home. I also got to meet amazing classmates. Definitely, the best decision I've ever taken. I ABSOLUTELY suggest it.

Don’t come unless you want to listen to the same 3 minute audio over and over and over and over again. Seriously each day consists of listening to a 3 minute audiotrack, discussing it, and then repeating the process for an hour. There’s no formal grammar taught, no reading or writing is allowed in class, in theory it’s supposed to help you listen and speak more but it’s so repetitive, and because there’re so anti book learning it’s frustrating and  waste of money. It’s also extremely expensive being one of the most expensive in Rome. I’ve attended several schools in Rome and have settled on Kappa. They’re a small school with a nice mix of class activities, talking and listening, grammar, etc, and for a much better cost.

I've spent one month in Rome studying italian language and culture at DILIT; it was a great choice: the teachers and DILIT team are very patient and make it easier to learn. The structure of the school is also amazing: good space to learn and to spend time with your friends (believe me, you make a lot in DILIT). If you want to have an excellent time in Rome, learning italian language, culture and making friends, choose DILIT!

I attended DILIT for many weeks/ months, unfortunately, the course and the school itself were quite disappointing. But first about the good points:

- Good Location, nice building and AC in summer
- Cafe in the basement, prices are okay for rome
- many Internationals and diverse mix which is nice for older people as well, not only for young 15-75+ years old (yes there are also many Pensioners in my group and others)

But of course I came to improve my Italian, unfortunately I got disappointed, in the following you can read why:

While there are some teachers who genuinely try to push the lessons forward, not all of them are like this. I had five different teachers in total. Roberto, for example, was quite good, but the others—I won’t mention names—seemed to just sit there. When you asked them something, you could feel they were just waiting for the time to pass. It’s also frustrating that the teachers change so often, which disrupts continuity.

The price is completely overpriced for what you get. You won’t really learn much because you only end up speaking with other students who make the same mistakes as you. There’s barely any correction, and the teachers don’t really teach vocabulary or grammar. I know people who complained about this. Some paid over €4,000 because they were really serious about learning the language. No surprise, they burned out, were allowed to leave the school earlier, and were offered a refund or some other compensation.

For anyone considering a language course, I would strongly advise learning by yourself. Get a private teacher, practice vocabulary and grammar—things this school definitely doesn’t focus on. I recommend the app Busuu (get the premium subscription for about €90; it offers structured lessons and other useful features, and you can easily reach A2 level). It’s way better than Duolingo. I also recommend the YouTube channel "Passione Italiana" where you can learn grammar and how to use it effectively. Listening to podcasts is another great way to improve.

To put this in perspective, I’m also learning German as a third language at the Goethe Institute for the same price. There’s absolutely no comparison in what you learn there in the same time and for the same money.

If you combine these tips, you will definitely learn Italian faster and better! Really, some people pay €2000 for a 4-week course, but they end up speaking Italian at the same level as me after using the resources I listed.

In summary:

- My criticism is mainly directed at those teachers who just sit there and don’t engage.
- My advice to students is to learn by yourself, and once you reach A2 with the resources I mentioned, get a private teacher and just keep speaking.
- This school is absolutely overpriced for what you get. The price might be fair if you weren’t sitting in a class of 15 students, all of whom are speaking as poorly as you, and where your mistakes aren’t corrected.

Great experience of studying for a month here. Amazing Teachers (Milena was our teacher, I will definitely recommend her ), fantastic and friendly staff, very cosy atmosphere, and here is another bit- a  brilliant cafe 😀 with delicious food and gentle owners. Thank you !

Highly recommend Dilit International house! The location is great and the staff and teachers are extremely professional! Assistance is alway there regardless how small and the teachers go above and beyond to ensure the school meets your individual needs. The school’s proactive teaching method and structured learning provided me with a great framework to build my language skills and adjust my expectations when learning a language. I spent six weeks learning Italian in Dilit international house and at first the method may seem daunting but the school provided me with great learning tools to continue to develop improving my Italian!  Thank you to my teachers Antonella and Francesca!!
Great school, but I thought it was just a legendary palace. Hope in Babylonia will build it
I myself went to school here for three months and had a very good experience. Nice teachers, no nonsense, extra-curricular opportunities if you want them. Recommended.
In case you are looking for perfect language school, choose Torre di Babele. Quick progress, professional and friendly teachers and a lot of fun :)

I liked the school because it had a great building and my teacher was lovely, funny and beautiful. The lessons were pleasant. Organisation was good. Perfect for tourists who want to practice some italian. I will go again in october.

If you want to learn Italian in Rome, this is the school where you can learn it!! I had two previous and very bad experiences, for my first two years on a student visa here, but then I found this school, and it is truly an amazing experience. THANK YOU Torre di Babele! I will learn and am finally learning Italian. The teachers (I have had five different teachers so far at different levels in different courses, and they, every single one of them, are outstanding. I too am a teacher, a teacher of English, and I know teaching methods. Not only do they use the most effective teaching methods, every single teacher is enthusiastic about their job, they speak clearly, no other language is spoken in the classroom, the school is utterly amazing. I highly recommend it. I regret my two previous, and very costly, mistakes in locating a school to learn Italian, but I am most grateful I found Torre di Babele.

I participated in Scuola Leonardo da Vinci’s Programma La Dolce Vita, spending two weeks in Viareggio, one week in Turin, and one week in Rome as part of a month-long Italian immersion experience.

I did not grow up speaking Italian, but the language has always been part of my family’s story. My grandparents spoke the Ciociarian dialect, and my mother, aunt, and uncle grew up hearing and speaking it as well. My grandfather was from Ceprano, Lazio, and my great-grandparents were from Sant’Ambrogio sul Garigliano. I am studying Italian as part of my journey toward Italian citizenship and to reconnect with my heritage.

My week at Scuola Leonardo da Vinci Roma was the highlight of the entire program.

Rosanna was an exceptional teacher. Her classes were engaging, fun, and incredibly effective. She created an environment where students felt comfortable participating and learning. Of the four weeks I spent studying in Italy, my week with Rosanna was my favorite. Honestly, I wish I had spent my entire month in Rome.

I would also like to thank Caterina, my tutor, who was patient, encouraging, and genuinely invested in my success. Every session was productive, and she gave me confidence to continue learning.

Cinzia in the office was welcoming and helpful, and Andrea’s pasta-making class was a wonderful cultural experience. I also preferred the textbook used in Rome and found it the most user-friendly of the three locations.

The true test came after the program ended. During my fifth week in Italy, I traveled to my family’s ancestral towns to gather records and correct documents for my citizenship application and family genealogy research. Thanks to what I learned at Scuola Leonardo da Vinci, I was able to introduce myself, explain my purpose, and hold basic conversations at the comune offices. For someone who arrived as a complete beginner, that was incredibly rewarding.

Studying abroad is a significant investment, but Scuola Leonardo da Vinci Roma made every euro worthwhile. I plan to continue studying online and hope to return before taking the B1 CILS exam.

This school helped me do more than learn Italian—it helped me connect more deeply with my family’s history, heritage, and future.
Brilliant experience doing a week's beginner's course. Daniela was a fantastic and engaging teacher, the whole course was very well organised and I thoroughly enjoyed it.

I completed a 2-week intensive B1 course in Rome.  Overall, I did learn a lot, but there were many things they could improve on, or that weren’t geared toward a short-term, older student.

- When I arrived early for my first class, I was told that my class time was unexpectedly changed from 12:00-3:15 to 3:30-6:45pm. I was lucky that I could accommodate this last-minute, unannounced change for the entire 2 weeks of my course.
- Since the Placement Exam is all online, there is no consideration given as to how well you can understand spoken Italian. I wasn’t informed in advance of where I was placed.
- There was no orientation, or introduction to the school given to me when I arrived. Just directions to “go up the stairs and find classroom E”.
- I was not told about the extra activities, nor about the WhatsApp group that distributed information on the activities. I learned about those in week 2. That was disappointing.
- I didn’t know they had a library that was open to students for studying.
- The teacher didn’t introduce herself to me nor introduce any of the other students in class (there were about 14 students in class), as they had clearly been together for weeks/months and I was the only new student.  It did not feel welcoming.
- In general, it seems that most students are 18-30 yrs old, begin classes with other friends or else have been studying at the school for a long time, so the atmosphere wasn’t set up to welcome a single, older short-term student.
- There was a final exam given at the end of the 2 week course, but I have no idea how I performed in relation to expectations.
- I had to request a certificate of completion from them weeks later, as once my class ended, there was no contact made with me nor follow-up.

In short, they treated a short-term student as simply a transaction — tuition was paid & a seat was made available in a classroom for me.

I just returned from a week's intensive course in Torino and I now properly understand the true value of full immersion learning.  I've been studying Italian now for 10 years, but in reality only the last 2 with proper daily effort.  Yet I was still stuck in the intermediate quagmire, with decent B1.2 grammar understanding and pronunciation, but let down totally with my poor listening ability.
For that reason, I was very apprehensive about a 100% Italian course, and also learning with young folks as a mature student.  My fears were totally unfounded.  My teacher Antonietta spoke loudly and clearly at an even pitch, and facilitated the class with logical/sequential explanations on the blackboard for any points of difficulty.
We spoke barely 10 words of English all week.
Old school style workbook/blackboard teaching, but very effective.  It was like a turbocharger on my ear and comprehension.  I partook in every extra evening/afternoon activity, which further improved my conversation skills.
One evening dinner with other students I was stunned how was keeping up with Andrea's fast speech after 3 days and for the first time I felt confident to speak with Italian in shops and restaurants.
Torino is not a full-on international tourist town- wall to wall Italian - but is really nice and easy to get around with lots of history to get involved in.  The school is also conveniently centrally located.
Stop procrastinating and researching.  Just do it.  I only wish I had more time for a few more weeks to consolidate everything and I will return for a longer stint if I can manage it.

Probably the best experience in my life. The decision about coming to this school has brought a lot of wonderful memories and new friendships. I've spent in Rome 4 beautiful weeks (july/august) and definitely i'm going to go back there. I had lessons with Ida, Andrea, Caterina and Julia and finally i've stopped to be afraid of speaking in italian. There is still a lot of work for me but already it gave me a lot!
Natalia

I attended this school for two weeks and appreciated the opportunity to practise Italian every day. The atmosphere was friendly, and speaking in class helped build my confidence.

However, I felt the lessons could be more structured. Classes often started a few minutes late, and I would have liked more detailed explanations of grammar, with examples written on the board rather than mainly following the textbook.

I also felt that some teachers were more patient and engaging than others. When learning a new language, a supportive and encouraging teaching style makes a big difference.

Overall, it was a good experience, but there is room for improvement in organisation and teaching consistency.

I studied here to prepare for and pass my B1 citadinaza. I started from zero, and after only two and a half months of studying, I was able to pass. I studied independently also , but the teachers were always supportive and helped me with additional exercises and assignments outside of class. I had a great time in this school!

I had a very enjoyable two weeks at Accademia StudioItalia language school. I did the Intensive Plus and found the balance between small class learning with a mix of grammar, italian culture, reading and speaking in the two morning sessions and the 1:1/1:2 conversation class in the afternoon really helped me progress my ability to communicate in Italian. All the teachers and staff are extremely experienced and supportive, as were my fellow classmates.  Two weeks is too short, of course, but I plan to return again and without any doubt my Italian is better now than it was.  Also, the school is in Prato, a very pleasant and not to busy part of Rome; a perfect base for exploring the city in the afternoons/evenings.

My time at Accademia StudioItalia has been far more than just a language course, it has been a truly transformative experience. I felt welcomed into a supportive environment where learning Italian didn’t feel like an obligation but a joy.

I give my greatest respect and compliments to my teacher, Chiara. She is not only highly skilled but also deeply passionate about what she does. She brings energy, patience and genuine care into every lesson that makes the most challenging aspects of the language feel approachable. What I appreciated most is her ability to connect with each student and adapt her teaching in a way that makes everyone feel confident and included.

I’m deeply grateful for everything this school has given me and I would recommend it wholeheartedly to anyone looking for a meaningful and enriching language learning journey.

xx Jhoanna xx

I loved this school so much when I studied Italian here for a week in 2023 that I came back for a month in October 2025. Which I loved even more! Wonderful teachers (Marco, Ludovica, and Livio were each ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️), useful content, fast-paced lessons that can be extended with optional homework, moltissimo fun. Students are motivated adult learners from all over the world, so the classroom environment is incredibly rich and stimulating—both intellectually and personally. I learned so much, made real friends (❤️❤️ A1 ottobre 2025!), and am very sad to leave! Molto grazie e c’è vediamo pronto, Accademia Studioitalia!

I am writing a review after 1 month of learning Italian at Kappa Language School, and I can honestly say that I had a very positive experience.

Before choosing a school in Rome, I spent a long time comparing different options. For me, it was important to find a school with: an intensive course, reasonable prices, and morning classes.

Kappa Language School matched all of these criteria perfectly.

I attended the beginner intensive course from Monday to Friday, 9:00–11:00. After one month of classes, I can say that I really enjoyed everything: the selection of topics, the location, my group, and most importantly, the teacher.

Our main teacher was Francesca Sorrentino— a wonderful person and a talented teacher. The 2-hour lessons were never boring. The material was rich and well-structured, with a great variety of activities during class. Another thing I really appreciated was that the lessons were entirely in Italian — she never switched to English, even with beginners. I think this was extremely helpful and made the learning experience much more immersive.

Thank you so much, Francesca!

The only thing I would improve is adding air conditioning to the classroom where we studied, because during the summer it gets quite hot.

Overall, I would definitely recommend this school to anyone looking for an Italian course in Rome.

Kappa is a wonderful place to learn Italian.
It’s a smaller school and after trying several schools and then settling here with a student visa, I’m happy with my choice and usually leave each day feeling positive and happy about my progress and class.

The teachers and staff are all friendly, supportive, and super patient with a relaxed atmosphere and they use a variety of methods to help you learn and I feel they meet each student where they’re at.
In particular Gloria is a phenomenal and enthusiastic teacher. She makes the class and learning fun and the time goes by super quick!

I highly recommend Kappa if you want to learn Italian, and also need a student visa, as they really help walk you through the process of attaining one!

Joining Kappa language school has been so far one of my best decisions here in Rome. I studied italian (mostly by myself) for a couple of months but I wanted to give it more structure so I asked to join a course there for 1 month. Based on a short basic initial conversation they told me which level I am and I could choose in what time I would like to attend classes (either in the morning or afternoon). My teacher Francesca is awesome, very energetic and she pushes you (in the best way) to get better. She talks only in italian, but she makes sure it’s easy for everybody to understand. Can only highly recommend!

I’ve been studying at this school for 5 months and I’m very happy with my experience.
The teacher, Gloria, is amazing and always gives 100% during the lessons.
The classes are engaging and well-structured.
I actually relax and recharge during the lessons, which makes learning even more enjoyable.
The atmosphere is very pleasant, and the staff is always helpful and supportive.
I highly recommend this school!

Kappa is a terrific language school. I attend classes whenever I get a chance to have time free from work. The classes are very well structured and the instructors have a lot of energy and they keep us all talking which very important as often in language courses there is not enough opportunity for the students to speak.  The classes are small , usually no more than 6 or 7 people, and they include people of all ages and from various parts of the world and we become friends. I have taken classes from 3 different instructors and they are all exceptional teachers  their enthusiasm is really clear and they constantly invent new ways to engage the students. I have recommended this school to 3 friends and they all tell me how much they enjoy coming here and how quickly they are learning. The school is located in a very nice, lively area of  Rome and is easy to get to on public transportation.

Five stars does not begin to capture what Scrudit Rome has given our son.. What an incredible place.

Over the past three weeks, our son attended your school and what he received was so much more than language lessons. He found inspiration, kindness, encouragement, laughter, and memories that will stay with him for life.

From the wonderful Principal, whose warmth and constant positivity seem to shape the spirit of the entire school, to the incredible teachers who care so deeply for their students thank you. You have created something truly special.

A special mention as well to Bruno and Luca, we heard so many funny stories and joyful moments about you both. Those little memories are often the things that stay with people forever.

We are also deeply grateful to Alessia for all the information provided, from the very first email to Scrudit Rome. Because of her everything went to incredibly smooth, and he experienced something unforgettable.

What stands out most is not only the quality of teaching, but the humanity of everyone involved. There is a warmth, joy and genuine care in this school that is rare to find.

Our son has already said he hopes to return in future summers and honestly, we understand why.

Thank you for giving young people not just language skills, but confidence, connection and experiences they will carry for life.

Please never lose what makes this place

If you like a school with very traditional teaching and a fixed learning style, this may be the school for you.

If, on the other hand, you thrive best with dynamic teaching in a safe atmosphere that allows for you to learn in different ways, you should choose another school. There are many good schools that also offer outdoor and indoor environments that invite you to get to know other students.

I had requested a specific level in advance and had been confirmed that there was a class at that level.
When we arrived on monday morning, we were asked to fill out a test. We then waited for 45 minutes before a nice teacher came and started teaching us without looking at the test. We therefore all ended up in the same class, even though we had quite different levels. We were not given an introduction to the school, the social activities or anything else.

Some of us learn best by writing notes and looking through topics frequently to make connections and new understandings. However, taking notes or looking at previous notes was not allowed by the teacher during class, which I do not think is appropriate for adults who can decide for themselves how to best retain the new learning.

Our teacher seemed impatient - and yet she was both knowledgable, experienced and ambitious. She introduced us to several interesting and relevant topics; italian politics, religion, culture, food, daily life etc., which I liked.

I met the professor for a few minutes, and he seemed very nice and fun.

I cannot recommend this school highly enough! Having moved to Rome permanently, I have spent between 8-12 weeks (on and off) taking a mix of group and private lessons with various of the school's fantastic teachers.

All of the teachers are incredibly passionate and engaging. I had the pleasure of working with many of the teachers - from Luca, Alessandra, Alessandro, and Chiara - and the standard of teaching is exceptional, personalised and great value for money. Further, Alessia runs a great office, always on hand to ensure your schedule is organised and you have what you need (including that you take advantage of the various packages on offer to keep your costs down).

Learning a new language can be a daunting experience but there is a real family feel to the school and I was made to feel incredibly welcome. About 3 years ago I took a group course for 6 weeks at an alternative school in Monti, and didn't enjoy it to the same extent as my recent experience.

The school itself is situated in a beautiful location in San Giovanni and easy to reach. In addition, subject to student numbers, the school also runs various free events on a weekly basis, ranging from lectures / discussions on relevant Italian topics, to excursions at some of Rome's most beautiful sites.

I was placed in a level too advanced for me. I could have asked for changing but I did not, the teacher mainly interacted with one student, it was mainly conversation for 3 hours and half, the teacher said what she had to say in front of other students without being very aware she was hurtful. I was a stressful experience. But I improved slightly, so I give a star for this!

I was at the scudit language school for round about 3 months after my brother has spend a fair amount of time at the same language school. I am half Italian, while not being able to speak the language. However, after the 3 months I was able to have a conversation, which was definitely not perfect considering my grammar, but I had an aweful lot of fun learning.  The school gave me a great basis to continue my Italian. Additionally, they continously organized tours with the entire langauge school to visit and understand the great history behind Rome. Overall, I can only highly recommend Scudit, as it feels like a family while being there.

I am a retired American who attended Ciao Italia for the month of April 2024.  I was in the B1 intensive course.  My classes were small (5 students or less counting myself) and the students' ages varied considerably, which was nice.  My instructors were excellent: I had Marta for grammar and Marco for conversation.  The office staff was available and responsive. The school is in the interesting Monti neighborhood.  Find the time to improve your Italian by attending this good school for a least one month.

It was an incredibly enriching time in Rome. The combination of your language school “CiaoItalia”and this antique city is first-class. Your language school is pleasantly familiar and at the same time very professional. The two teachers I had, Simona  and Marco, are from Rome and put 100% of their energy into the Italian language. They speak clearly, loudly and at the right speed (neither too fast nor too slow). They also have a great sense of humour, so learning in a group is fun and not boring. Thank you so much for that great experience. I will come back!!!
Yours sincerely,
Assunta

It was my second time at Ciao Italia. As it was a few years before, I went for the Italian language course in Italy for one month on my vacation time. And it was just great! Everything, from the beginning both times, was very well organized and the answers and the information were always provided super quickly, and I had no additional stress, so my special thanks go to Alessia for the amazing work that she has done… The school is located in the city center - very near the famous Colosseum and everything else is just around. The classes at the school are small and everyone there is super friendly and nice. The teachers were the best I had ever had. Simona – is the grande virtue of conversation class whit the great passion and capacity to meet everyone’s needs and to create a special atmosphere by bringing together those very international students.  And Marco is definitely the best expert in grammar that even I, who really dislike grammar in any language, could understand and even be motivated to do the homework which I never did before in my Italian language studies... I could say that I have so many laughs and fun, an amazing time whit amazing people plus a high level of knowledge of the Italian language, history, culture, attitude, living here possibilities, and many recommendations of where to go for the meal, what events, museums, and places are interesting to visit in the city and In Italy in general. So, I want to thank everyone for this amazing experience, and I definitely want to come back as soon as possible 😊

After I arrived in Rome, I visited three different schools in person before choosing Ciao Italia. It was painfully obvious which one was the right pick. After encounters with distant secretaries and staff that only produced half-answers to my inquiries, Ciao Italia was the first place that felt truly warm and honest. I was met by Silvia, the headmistress herself, who not only answered all my questions but also kindly offered me assistance and advice (not to mention a great price) on my Italian learning journey. After our talk, she took me on a tour of the school which is small and intimate and let me meet the class that I would ultimately become a part of. Suffice to say that for a nervous girl in foreign territory, that meeting left me feeling like the pieces were falling into place.
I’ve now spent four months at the school and have met almost all of the staff. The teachers are some of the warmest, kindest people I have met, brilliant and considerate. In class, they always make you feel comfortable enough to laugh, chitchat and make mistakes. The classes are small with lots of opportunities to ask questions and practice speaking and after hours, there are activities of different kinds to try, ranging from Italian movie showings to cooking courses. At Ciao Italia I have gone from having a literal two-word vocabulary to speaking Italian at B1-level in only 4 months. And I’ve had so much fun doing it!
So, in essence, if you’re looking for a good Italian school in Rome, this is your lucky day. Once you go Ciao Italia, you never go back!

I spent a week in Rome at Ciao Italia doing an intensive course and I learned so much in just one week. The location of the school in the Monti area is kind of amazing to say the least. Because of "lockdown" I have been able to continue classes online with the school for the last 8 months and I cannot recommend them highly enough. The teachers are all really interested in their students and love what they do. We study in small groups and the classes are a very happy space. I have made friends for life and can have a real conversation in Italian.

Attended classes as an older adult along with mixed age and many college students.  I only wish there was an exact replica of the school in the USA.  Classes were taught all in Italian which may sound scary but absolutely the best way to get it done.  I chose the five days a week 3+hour a day for about 2 months and then two days a week for about a month.  This was in 2017 and I was really happy with progress and got along pretty well speaking and understanding during my year long stay in Rome.  Every instructor was better than the next.  Some of the teaching styles varied but all effective and the switch up every few weeks I think was great.  Administrators are very helpful too.  Recommend this school 1000%   I miss them all.

Studied abroad in Rome for a month with my school and went to Italiaidea. Flo is AMAZING! Love her so much! Even when she was absent though, all of the professors there were fantastic. Great teachers, informative on both the language and the city, and just downright super nice people. They also have extracurricular activities like pasta making and soccer that you sign up for at the school with other students and it's an amazing experience overall. GO HERE!

I had a wonderful experience at Italiaidea. After a month-long intensive course with Luigi I can read and understand most of the Italian I encounter. The classroom was a fun space and many of the events organized by the school were wonderful additions to my Italian experience. I wholeheartedly recommend Italiaidea.

What a great school!  By design, I had a combination of several teachers and while they all had different styles they were all great and put good emphasis on not only grammar but also practice in speaking, listening to recorded dialogues (which for me is the hardest - thank you for making me do this!), and writing.  In addition to the teachers, I must also compliment the administration: not only are they incredibly responsive and get back to you immediately with answers (which is not a given here in Italy), but they are also very supportive.  For example, when tourist season ended and my advanced class came down below the minimum size of 4 students, they allowed us to keep going at the same cost and schedule with only 2 students for several weeks before we transitioned to a different schedule.  Whenever I paid by-the-day rates, if I was absent a particular day they just credited me the amount (or in my case, let me use the paid day for the following week).  And finally, when my daughter's school was closed for a strike they had no problem with my 6-yr-old daughter coming along for class - she even got to be the teacher's assistant (and ever since then keeps asking her own teacher when the next strike is so that she can come with me to Italidea again....).  Highly recommended!
I was very happy to study in Italiaidea. It helped me a lot to achieve a better understanding of Italian language and the teachers helped me a lot.
I studied there when an Au Pair in Rome and was impressed by the teaching- highly qualified staff and perfect location near my beloved Pantheon

I was there for 1 month of intensive lessons, with a B1 level. I enjoyed following these lessons, which had a lot a grammar, which I needed, but also offered some time to improve our speaking skills.
The teachers are really good and the staff is very available for our questions.
The only flaw regards how they evaluate our level at the beginning : the test only questioned our grammar level, they didn't seek to speak with us in Italian before assigning us to the group level, thus for the first week I was a bit bored in my group.
All in all, there is still room for improvement in their organisation but I feel I've really improved my Italian as much as I expected to !

Best experience ever. Got in touch with the school, got immediate advice on what to do and which course to book. Very prompt and professional. Arriving in Rome, I had a swift test to determine my level and then started my 2 week course to brush up my Italian. All very well organised, high standard of teaching. I'm returning to ancient languages ​​as an adult, and I find the Institute online. I'm intrigued by the description of the method, directly in the language, and I sign up. This is an excellent place to learn Italian. My girlfriend and I are travelling Italy for a month, so we decided to enroll in this school for the two weeks we stay in Milan. We took a test and they placed us in classes at each appropriate level. She has been studying Italian for a while but I only took a few lessons, so I was place at a beginner level class and she was placed on a slightly advanced one. The class I joined had started for 3 weeks but I think I was able to catch up. I recommend joining at the start of a course if possible, but if you already have some basic knowledge you can probably join in the middle without too many problems. Classes are divided in two 90 minutes part with a 15 minute interval good enough to go get a quick coffee at the nearby bar.  I had two different teachers (M-W-F / T - T), both were excellent although each with a slightly different style. I liked them both. One was a bit more structured and the other was a bit all over the place which I particularly enjoyed a lot. When you join the class they give you a book which is hardly used during class, but this is actually great since the book is perfect if you like to go over the topics at home. Each chapter starts with grammar , follow by exercises (with answers on the back) and two quick tests at the end of the chapter... being an engineer I really like this structured approach. Classes on the other end are usually based on photocopies which are a bit more diverse. On each class you interact with the other students to complete assignments. This forces you to use the knowledge you got on the lecture and practice a bit. They give you some homework like writing essays or complete some exercises but not a lot and you can do it fairly quickly.
After a few weeks you take a standardized test to measure if you can pass to the next level or not. The test was not too difficult... you need to study but it is not something that requires memorizing words or grammar.. it is fairly natural.
All and all, I would advise anyone to choose this school if you are in Milan and want to learn Italian. Since I was here for only 2 weeks I can't say anything about Student Visas requirements or how the school handles that, but every one in administration seem like very professional and eager to help. Classrooms were fine, the one I was in had a computer with a large screen so we could do more dynamic stuff like learning a song  or do some grammar games. We were at most 7 students so it was not crowded. Students are from all over the world and from diverse ages. They were all very friendly.

My two week experience at this school -- which attracts students from all ages and from around the world --  was absolutely exceptional. The teachers are all top notch, with excellent lesson plans, a variety of approaches (conversation, grammar) and really effective and personalized methods. The location is in the historic center of Bologna, a fantastic city that's close to so many other historic sites and cities. And the school continues its education offerings after classes with a variety of  events (walks and longer hikes, city tours, aperitivi, gelato exploration, weekend trips to cities like Parma, Ferrara, Modena, etc... and even a fantastic cooking school offered twice a week). All this makes Cultura Italiana Bologna a perfect destination to immerse yourself in Italian culture and language studies. Can't speak highly enough for this great organization. I'll be back next year!

The school also helped to organise my accommodation.
I will be returning in the future for the next levels.

10/10 experience. I stayed in bologna with the school for four months. I had an AMAZING time, so much fun at the school, plus learnt heaps of italian. What’s more, the classes are fun. We played games, we told anecdotes, we worked solo and in duos and trios. I spent a decent portion of every day at Madrelingua laughing. I was always excited about going to class.

Another strength of the Madrelingua program is the social interaction. Each day classes are broken into two parts, separated by a half hour or so at a local cafe with your class and instructor or instructors so the chitchat is all in Italian and it’s fun.  Then, in the afternoon when classes are over, the school offers field trips to sights of interest, pasta-making lessons, exercise sessions or apertivi evenings with local Italian friends of the school.
I can’t recommend Madrelingua enough. It’s a special place. You feel like part of a community full of smart people who like to laugh.

My husband and I visited several language schools in Verona, but L’Italiano con noi was the only one where we truly felt welcome. Giorgia, the owner of the school, took time for us, explained everything and from the very first moment we could feel the friendly and relaxed atmosphere. That was one of the main reasons why we chose this school, and we are very happy that we did.

The lessons were fun, dynamic and we learned a lot through games, activities and especially conversation — not only grammar. In 8 months we reached a B2 level, but even more important for us was that we got to know not only Italian culture and history, but also wonderful people from all over the world.

Besides regular lessons, the school also organizes many activities outside the classroom — guided city tours, wine tastings or pasta-making workshops.

Another bonus is the perfect location right in the historical center of Verona, close to Piazza delle Erbe. During breaks we often went for coffee to nearby cafés and sometimes we even had lessons there :)

Thank you so much!
