All the teachers are professional, friendly, and experienced. During our 8 months here, we had lessons with Giancarla, Elena, Maurizio, and Giorgia herself.

If you are looking for a place where you can really learn Italian and enjoy the atmosphere at the same time, this is the place to be. The school also organizes many activities, from city tours to wine tastings and cooking events.

We were also very lucky because our groups were small, and we met wonderful people from all over the world.

We are extremely thankful that we found this school on our walk to Piazza della Erbe. And as a bonus, there is even a Starbucks nearby, where we sometimes had lessons :)

Spending a few weeks at L´Italiano con noi was an experience I will never forget. From the very first moment, I felt so welcome. The teachers and Giorgia (the director) greeted me with warmth and genuine interest, making me feel at home right away.

At L´Italiano con noi learning is not just about grammar and vocabulary, it’s about using the language in real life. The teachers are not only friendly and enthusiastic but also highly professional. They are experienced, well-prepared, and know exactly how to adapt to each student. Every lesson felt personal, with plenty of attention to my progress and questions. This made me feel supported and confident in improving my Italian.

Out of all the great activities the school organizes. My favorite one was the trip to Padova. The whole day was a perfect mix of learning, sightseeing and using the language. It’s a trip I will never forget!

At the end of my course, I didn’t just leave with better Italian, I also left with amazing memories, experience and new friends from all over the world.

Thank you all so much! :)

I had a great experience studying at L’Italiano con noi. The teachers are great and provide a lot of personal attention. Also the excursions and activities in the city are so much fun and give an opportunity to practice Italian in real-life situations. The location of the school is in the heart of the historic centre of Verona, which is a really big advantage and makes the experience even more special. Overall the atmosphere is very welcoming and I would definetly recommend the school to anyone!

I *LOVE* this school.  I had a wonderful experience in my B2 class, and I just wish I could have stayed for more than one month.   My teacher, Mattia, was excellent.  Incredibly clear explanations, and very patient.  Content was well-presented and classes were engaging and fun.  I've also had lessons with Davide, another great teacher at the school.  I am really impressed with the level of teaching here.

An added bonus was getting to know other students and making some new friends from around the globe, including  students from other classes during the extra afternoon activities.

Finding a place to stay was easy, since Federica arranged it all - and wow - what a fabulous apartment!  Walking into the school each day was a pleasure, being greeted with smiles from Elisa and Federica.

There is so much to see and do in Padova, and the school is centrally located - a very short walk to the historic center, botanic garden, museums, churches, cafés, restaurants, shopping... everything.

I highly recommend this school, and next time I'll be sure to sign up for more than just one month!

The Bertrand Russell School is ideally situated in the centre of Padua and, after morning lessons, it is easy to wander through the city sight seeing.  The staff at the school are pleasant and helpful.  You are thoroughly tested before attending to ensure that you are in an appropriate class, however, if you need to change groups it can be easily done.
There were five of us in my class; a good number because you had plenty of opportunities to speak which is what I wanted above all.  The work was at the right level for me; I was stretched and I did learn.  There was homework, too, which I also appreciated.  The teacher was excellent, (I was a teacher myself for over thirty years so I do have some experience of how to do it!).
My only disappointment was that a planned excursion did not take place because there were not enough interested people.  Ah well, maybe next year.  I was only there for a week, mainly out of curiosity, but my appetite for further language study has been whetted.

If you are looking to i prove your Italian, AND ready to take it seriously I couldn't recommend this school more.
The teachers are super friendly and professional. Mattia, Chiara, Anna, Davide and others were all very friendly, ready to help, answer questions even after school hours. This amazing team lifted me from absolute zero to a solid B2 level in 6 months.

Especially Mattia xoxo

I took a month-long intensive B1 course at Bertrand Russell Language School in Padova, and it was an excellent experience. My teacher, Mattia, was fantastic! He was engaging, patient, and extremely skilled at breaking down difficult concepts in a clear way. The classes were well-structured, interactive, and genuinely enjoyable.

I also arranged my accommodation through the school, which was incredibly easy!

I highly recommend Bertrand Russell Language School, especially if you have the chance to study with Mattia!

I've studied in the institute whole year in 2015 - 2016. In the addition to a high professional level the institute had an atmosphere of respect, friendship and joy! I was interested in learning. A wonderful team of teachers and assistants, which created a feeling of family. Kristina Garden, the principal of the institute is his soul. Still interested in each other's lives.

recensioni.autore: Marcel Leeb Systemisches Coaching in freier Natur
recensioni.testo:
I spontaneously decided to take a language course in Trieste. Everything was organized within 24 hours, including a lovely apartment provided by the school.

Communication and organization beforehand with Carlotta and Martina were straightforward and very friendly. They were incredibly dedicated to ensuring everything ran smoothly in the short time before the start.

The oral language test via Zoom was also very professional, straightforward, and friendly. I felt warmly supported by Claudia, who helped me find the right course and the best level for me.

And when I started the language course there on Monday, it continued in exactly the same way. I felt warmly welcomed and well supported from the very beginning.

A heartfelt thank you to Enza, who taught us the grammar with great enthusiasm and her wonderful sense of humor. A huge thank you also to Mirka for her incredible patience in helping beginners like us speak a new language fluently. It worked out very well for me.


The language school is located in a very beautiful and vibrant neighborhood with lovely cafes, restaurants, and small shops—a true taste of la dolce vita after class. And my apartment was just a 3-minute walk from the school in this same trendy area.

Many thanks to everyone who made my stay so wonderful.

Grazie mille di tutto,

Marcel

I cannot recommend Mariana’s Italian class highly enough. She is an incredibly talented teacher — patient, encouraging, engaging, and genuinely passionate about helping her students learn. Every class felt welcoming and thoughtfully organized, and Mariana has a wonderful ability to make even difficult concepts approachable and enjoyable.

What stood out most to me was her kindness and positivity. She creates an environment where students feel comfortable participating and making mistakes, which makes learning so much easier and more enjoyable. Even with my demanding travel and work schedule, I always looked forward to class and appreciated how supportive and flexible she was throughout the process.

The school overall has also been fantastic to work with — professional, warm, and truly invested in their students’ experience. I am very grateful for the opportunity to learn with Mariana and fully intend to return for classes again in the future.

Highly recommend to anyone looking to learn Italian in a welcoming and high-quality environment!

- lessons are engaging, useful and well prepared
- friendly and welcoming atmosphere
- the teachers have an exceptionally broad experience and a considerable specialist knowledge. I deeply admired the high degree of commitment and motivation
- the school in Trieste is overall highly organized & very customer-oriented. The receptionists speak a lot of different languages.
- the school offers: apartments, transfers, excursions and various course types (group classes, private lessons, online classes etc.). Possible to prepare and take official exams (CELI, CILS)
- Trieste is a safe city, has a interesting history & many sightseeing opportunities as well as a fantastic bus system (App: Tpl Fvg). Also great train connections to visit other places like Venice, Palmanova, Udine etc. (App: Trenitalia)
- to be kept in mind: majority of the students are from german-speaking countries (Germany, Austria, Switzerland). The average age of the students is quite high (I met a lot of students 60+). If you consider to take an exam, I highly recommend to take private lessons.

I’m posting this again because the first time I posted it google never posted it.  They indicated it was a false review and I never attended the online classes or I was being paid to write a good review!  But indeed… I did complete my first online class through Piccola Universita Trieste. I was hesitant to take an online group class but Virginia was a fantastic instructor and the group was very kind and we learned a lot while having fun! All in all a great experience. Thank you! L Gervasi

Classes: the classes are great, the teachers are fantastic, they are really engaging and the class sizes are small so less chance to get left behind.

Accomodation: The accomodation was very clean but it was down near the beach which meant walking 204 steps (11 floors) straight up the cliff at least twice a day. I was exhausted by the end of the week and it meant arriving at class in the morning already tired and sweaty. The school didn’t give me a heads up about the steps either and made no apology for the situation “That’s just part of staying in Tropea”, but in my opinion an 11 floor climb should be disclosed at the time of booking. Also wifi was out for 2 days, no microwave, oven tripped the power and the bathroom smelt of sewage. Price was expensive for southern Italy and my apartment was the same price as those in the centre of town. Organise your own accomodation so you know what you are getting.

Administration: This area also lets down the school. I missed my first class because the school didn’t provide my class information clearly, it was just told to me in the noisey foyer (in Italian not English and not in writing). I was told it was my fault because I should have been able to understand the italian instructions. The school gave me an extra class to make up the one I missed but acted like they were doing me a huge favour by doing so. Any problems were never the schools fault and I found the lack of empathy upsetting. Also only one person speaks English so everything is communicated in Italian, if you are a beginner this will be very difficult.

Social Activities: I think this school is more social activities than other schools, it also helps that Tropea is a small town so you end up seeing other students when you are out and about. But once again, some info on the activities in English would be really helpful, I felt like I was always having to work hard to understand what I was signing up for and I had to ask other students who understood more Italian than I did.

Overall, I enjoyed Tropea, learned a lot from the classes and loved having a group of students to hang with but the problems left me feeling stressed most of the week. I think a lot could be improved with just some better communication. Despite the classes being great the accomodation and administration issues really spoilt the trip.

A great language school that I highly recommend!

Classes are organised by level, the classrooms are spacious, and the number of students per class is limited (between 5 and 9 for me), which allows you to progress faster.
Group lessons consist of two 1h30 sessions (with a 30 minutes break in the middle) with two different and fantastic teachers who are both patient, knowledgeable and kind. This creates a dynamic atmosphere.

In addition, the school offers very interesting excursions/cultural visits every afternoon from Monday to Thursday (already included in the fee - except for transportation).

I learned a lot during these three weeks, both linguistically and culturally! Thank you again to Marina, Lorenzo, Anna, Sandro, and Cyntia!

Amazing school with an amazing principal and teachers . Really enjoyed the language class . The teachers created such a comfortable environment for students to learn. Will always be grateful to have had the opportunity to attend here

As a Turkish citizen, a French and English student and a English teacher my self, İ found İstituto Venezia very useful, fun, friendly and more..
Located in City center, easy to reach from every spot, İnstituto has a lot to offer.
All the teachers were friendly, positif, trying everything to make join the students who are reluctant or not enthustiastic.
Students with different nationalities, colorful...
The thing which İ found the most important and useful is the trips, all the classes are in the morning, after the lessons, İnstituto organises trips all around Trieste, and they don't charge you for these, you only pay for the transport, foods and drinks you consume if you'd like to. (Unlike lots of schools woldwide which would charge you extra for the trips they organize in profit of their company) They have trips every evening, even if you miss some, you have the chance to join one another, For me, personally every trip was an unforgettible memory.

It was great to see some good reviews before joining but I didn't find the reviews helpful in deciding to study there so allow me to break it down for you:

I studied in Trieste for over three weeks and I can say this was one of the best language schools I've learned at and I've studied at many languages in lots of different countries (French, Hebrew, Spanish, and Indonesian). I started as a beginner and I've learned so much already. The classes were from 9-1030 with a 30 min break then 1030-12 so three hours of learning and never once did I feel bored. This is because the three teachers (Giovani, Lorenzo and Sandro) are engaging, knowledgeable, warm and efficient. Keep in mind, the lessons are all in Italian so it can be difficult to keep up if you are used to learning with help of your native language.

The program does a fantastic job balancing lectures, exercises and games. The exercises will not only help you speak and read but also improve your listening skills.

The program is super affordable and worth every penny. Highly recommend.

Just FYI - the phone number here goes to the Venice location, not Trieste.
Wonderfull staff especially massimo Brunzin I didn't obtain visa to study there but I would like to thank him for every thing greetings from egypt
Bad teachers , too strict rules, Only nazario is cool.
I wouldn't visit again

I recently enrolled in an Italian course at this institute, but unfortunately I was not satisfied with the teaching method. The lessons were mostly spent on unsupervised speaking or writing activities, without enough correction, explanation, or grammar support from the teacher. When students made mistakes, they were often not corrected, and questions were limited or not fully answered.
I expected a paid language course to provide proper guidance, structured teaching, and useful feedback. Since I felt I was not learning anything, I preferred to stop attending the class. I hope the institute takes this feedback seriously and improves the teaching approach for future students.
Nice 🙂 place to learn
Very good!

Excellent place to learn multi languages. Top instructors and well equipped classroom. Very informative, supportive and responsive office staff. Basic levels are free of cost. Top of line and accredited.
I'm happy to study
Hallo, Did you how much cost for 1 month,to learn Italian language.
Adorable
I think it's great, everyone is so nice, and you get qualified information. The pace of the course is just right! The teacher is fantastic and gives individual attention to each student!
Great courses for German. If you are not Italian you can have a huge discount too, 1/5th of the normal price.
Serious and concrete, even though the location is terrible to say the least. Well done.

I had to take a C2 level exam at this language center. The listening test was administered through a stereo system that had absolutely inadequate audio for the complex material required for a C2 level exam. In another similar exam, administered at a different center with adequate stereo equipment, I achieved the highest score in the listening test.
Excellent service, the teachers are very helpful, and the quality is excellent. The only thing is that I would add more languages, such as Asian ones (Chinese, Japanese, Korean, etc.).

A historic institution that has been offering language certifications for years. Staff are available with attractive offers throughout the year. Despite organizational challenges related to the Covid period, the staff found immediate solutions for members, accommodating every request.
Good organization: I took the DALF C1 French exam here, organized by the Alliance Francaise of Verona.
Excellent school, knowledgeable teachers, and very helpful teaching materials. Highly recommended.
It's okay.
Excellent school, well-prepared teachers who don't abandon struggling students. 👍.

I had a wonderful experience at this language school and highly recommend it to anyone looking for a fun, immersive way to learn Italian.
The teachers are passionate, knowledgeable, and genuinely care about their students' progress. The staff is kind, welcoming, and always willing to help.
The school also offers a variety of cultural activities throughout the week, which are both enjoyable and a great way to experience Italian culture while practicing the language.
I truly enjoyed my time here and would recommend it to students of all levels.
Wonderful experience! Ottima scuola! I learned SO much in 3 weeks of a B1 class. Friendly and well-organized. Torino was a fantastic city to immerse oneself in Italian.

Best Italian language school in Turin.

Nice friendly staff, good teachers, own made textbook, good location at the edge of the centre.
I like it how they also include Italian, Piemontese and Turin culture and history in the courses.

An big extra are the 2 excursions they organise every week and are included for free in the course.
And last but not least: Turin is a terrific city! Hospitable, open, not to touristic, nice atmosphere. Probably the most underrated city of Italy.

I learnt Italian here for a week in February and I was sad to leave.

The teacher knew what she was doing and you could see she loves her job.

It is a small school, which makes it also special. They want to be able to know all the students personally and they do, they connnect with them and gladly help them with what they need.

They offer coffee and tea on the break for free and you can get something sweet for less than 1 €.

There arw activities you can join every week: usually two a week, but in summer they might do more, when they have more students.

I also work in a Language School and it was fun to know that this school is also founded, managed and directed by three women 💪🏻.

If you like chocolate and are looking for a school to learn italian in Italy, I recommend Turin (beautiful city with amazing views!) and I definitely recommend this school!

Thank you !😃

Liebe Grüße,
A. Lopez

This was my second time in L'Italiano Porticando and I can really recommend the school. The classes are small, the place is incredibly friendly and students feel comfortable. I had Ilenia as my teacher this time and she was fabulous - super knowledgeable, always happy to help and incredibly friendly. The entire approach to teaching is great, there is only Italian spoken, but at the right level so that even people who are not yet fluent are able to follow and understand. There is just the right mixture of written exercises, grammar and speaking, and you can book an additional 3 hours of conversation altogether in the afternoon, twice weekly. The extra activities are really lovely and the walk around the city with is so informative - Laura really knows how to convey the history of Turin. I definitely hope to be back next year!

Choose this school, you will not regret it!

My language stay in Turin was an incredible experience from start to finish. The school is located right on Piazza San Carlo, one of the most beautiful squares in the city, and studying there every day with such stunning views made the experience even more special.

A special thank you goes to my professor, Ivan, who was an excellent teacher. His lessons were engaging, well-structured, and encouraging, helping me gain confidence in speaking Italian despite being a very humble A2. He created a welcoming classroom atmosphere and always took the time to support students individually, even if you are an absolute beginner.

The school staff were also outstanding. Everyone was friendly, professional, and incredibly helpful throughout my stay, whether assisting with practical matters or providing recommendations about the city and local culture.

One of the highlights was the activity programme. The guided activities were conducted entirely in Italian, which was fantastic for full immersion. It gave me the opportunity to practise the language in real-life situations while discovering Turin and meeting people from around the world.

I highly recommend this school to anyone looking to improve their Italian in a supportive, immersive, and inspiring environment. It was a memorable experience that exceeded my expectations. Then also the city itself is a hidden gem to be discovered!

This is a great school to study Italian. The school staff is very attentive and helpful. The instruction is top notch! The environment is supportive and friendly. Turin is a beautiful city, with a lot of history. Also, it does not have the extreme tourist scene that other more high profile Italian cities have, which I appreciate. The school is located in one of the nicest areas in the city.
I would highly recommend this school!

Ciao Italy in Turin (online classes are awesome too), has been one of the best experiences of my entire life. I've attended this branch's school since late July and now it's late January, so about 6 months in total and I can honestly say everyday has been rewarding. I started intensive classes at A2 and eventually went up to B2. I was allowed to go back down to A2 twice and now back to B1 twice with zero issues. All the teachers (even the ones I only met in passing) and the secretaries, including the director, treat everyone with kindness and patience. Thank you specifically to Chiara, Antonietta, Silvia, Sebastiano, Alessio, Silvana, Francesca and Beatrice. You all have really been amazing and so helpful at some point during my first six months here and from the bottom of my heart, I'm so grateful for everything (especially your patience). PLEASE consider attending this amazing school and the after school activities, too. Try to take chances, make new friends, be patient on your language journey and continue to make mistakes and then learn from them. Truly open yourself up to learning Italian and you won't regret it! I will only ever have good and positive things to say about my time here and the incredible people I met along the way, and by the grace of God, I had a lot of help by incredible people. Thank you everyone and may God bless you all! ❤️ 10/10 experience. Grazie di cuore a tutti per tutto. Le parole non possono descrivere quanto sono grata! 🙏❤️

We are a group of over 50 Taiwanese individuals studying Italian at Ciao Italy Language School. We’re enjoying a long stay in Turin, immersing ourselves in the local culture. The staff and teachers are very friendly and hospitable. The head principal is especially kind and supportive—she helps us flexibly arrange our after-school activities, making our experience even more enjoyable.

I was in the same La Dolce Vita class as the most recent reviewer and agree this school does a great job making students feel comfortable with the Italian language. You're challenged, but in positive ways. I'd had some trauma with language classes in the past - so I had anxiety on the first day - but it soon felt good and comfortable to be here. And it was great to learn some of the language, and to be set up for success in future studies both at home and hopefully in Turin again.  After a week with Stefania and the school, I left a really happy student of Italian.
We had hoped these studies would help us as we traveled another week in Italy, and indeed the school prepared us well - we were OK even when communicating with people who didn't speak English.
La Dolce Vita includes after-school activities which were also amazing and enriching. I'd encourage you to look at the images and videos on the Turin FB page. Not all students speak the same language, so of course the activities are in the native tongue taught at the school. The activities are entirely in Italian, and so for five evenings I was cognizant that I was missing 90+ percent of the content. That didn't matter as much as you might think because my wife and I had at least 80 percent of the fun. You don't get experiences like those at home.
And the sights you get to see both at school and in Turin - wow. I included a couple of photos, first of the plaza where the school is located and then a view from a classroom. The rest are a few photos from some of the activities in town.
That reminds me of a final point. Turin is not on the top of every English-speaking visitor's list; that's one reason why you should go. It's plenty busy, but it's not over-touristed. We found ourselves often surrounded by locals, not packs of tourists. Turin has as many or more cool buildings and sites as any major Italian city, and an incredibly rich history that rewards you at every turn. Yet we paid less here for accommodations than we would have paid in many other cities where people study Italian. Turin is a bargain with rich rewards.

5-stars all the way.  A Door to Italy is a great language school catering to all levels. The teachers and staff are very friendly and eager to help students along their journey to learn the Italian language.  The school has a valuable didactic approach to enable students to not only learn the grammar - but also practice how and when to use it.  And there is a very useful grammar handbook prepared by the school for all students full of useful examples.
The school is located centrally in Genoa.  The city is steeped in history and is a great 'door' to Italian culture and cuisine.  Genoa is an ideal location to explore all that Liguria has to offer.
Great school.  Great city.  Win - Win !!

I had a great experience at the school. The teachers and the staff are very friendly, helpful, and supportive. I had a two-week in-person intensive group class that was very engaging and fun. The school arranged accommodation for my brother and I in a beautiful apartment in very nice neighborhood conveniently located close to the school and major attractions. I would totally recommend the school and the experience.

This is an excellent school. The teaching is based on a Communicative approach where the teachers guide the discovery and practice of the language with an infectious enthusiasm, which extends beyond the language itself, to Italian culture in general and to Genova in particular. I felt that over my two weeks in Genova at the school, I made huge advances both in my language competence, and my confidence in speaking. I would have gladly stayed for much longer if had been possible. I recommend this school unreservedly.

I strongly recommend A Door to Italy to anyone interested in deepening their Italian language skills. From my initial contact with the school, through to my last day, the staff replied promptly to my inquiries, and eagerly assisted me with whatever I needed. The highly experienced teachers create a welcoming environment in which students from diverse backgrounds can practice listening to, writing, and speaking Italian. For a deep cultural immersion, I strongly recommend the allogia familiare housing option. You never know what host family you will get, but don’t worry, the school carefully screens all its families for fit and location. And because Genova is less well known than other tourist hotspots, you can explore the breathtaking Ligurian coast without ever hearing your native tongue. I am grateful to A Door to Italy for an unforgettable and immersive experience and I hope to study with them again soon.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

My experience at A Door to Italy was simply incredible. I studied there for only one month, but it made a huge difference in my life. I noticed a clear improvement in my Italian, and the school helped me feel more connected to the city through the extra activities and the small trips we did. It was also a great way to make friends, especially because everyone in my group had the same level of Italian, which made everything more enjoyable and motivating.

I truly have no words to thank the entire team for all the support, patience and kindness. It was the best experience I have ever had with a language school. They were absolutely wonderful. I recommend A Door to Italy with complete confidence, because it is an experience I will always remember. ❤️🥹

I studied 4 weeks at this school and stayed 4 weeks in student housing.  Great teachers and other staff members.  Everyone I interacted with was professional and kind.  I am glad I picked this school for my first experience with the Italian language.  A great experience.  Thank you!

Scuola Tricolore offers an extremely helpful, responsive and engaging language learning experience in a wonderful and accessible part of Genoa.

Communication in arranging tuition was very pleasant and reliable. An intensive course was also designed around my own availability which was particularly helpful and impressive. The school staff are also very passionate about various different languages and cultures - making this a fantastic point of entry for anyone wishing to have a genuine learning experience of the Italian language and Genoa itself!

I´ve been to many language schools in several countries, so I can compare the quality of the course and accomodation to others. First of all, I wouldn´t recommend this school for those who would like to improve the level of language and come to Italy to study. The course plan is VERY chaotic, I stayed for 1 month on A2 and we didn´t learn anything about verbs and tenses which is the most important thing on this level, at the same time we had much less important themes such as articles, pronouns etc., and the worst thing was that the teacher repeated some of them 3 times during the month. Another girl that stayed in the class for 2 months also said that they never studied the future tense, which is ridiculous not to know it after finishing A1-A2 level.

Another thing was accomodation which was not clean. The cleaning lady was coming to the appartment only if some new student was coming and instead of staying there for 2 hours she was cleasning 5 dorms flat in 30 minutes, just washing floor slightly (not everywhere) and kitchen. There was a lot of dust everywhere and mold in the bathroom. We have reported this to a school and got the answer that it was our responsibility to clean the coomon areas in the appartment which I believe is not fare taking into account the amount we were paying for it. And, of course, students who are coming for vacations for 2-3 weeks, would never care of this. Also this cleaning lady was supposed to give keys to new students, but she was never answering the phone where someone new was calling her to know the right address of the appartment or sth like this. So 2 of our flatmates had to stay in a hotel the first night due to her irresponsibility and of course the were not refunded by a school.

Scuola Tricolore is a great place to learn Italian.
The teachers are excellent, skilled at explaining new grammar concepts, and ensuring that a wide variety of topics are used to introduce new vocabulary.  They ensure full group participation in the lessons, as well as keeping them fun and interesting.
Richard and Rossana are so helpful, from the initial query, then hints and tips on what to do and where to go in Genova and Liguria, and finally to suggestions for an aperitivo on my last evening.  This made my stay so much more than a stay at an italian school, as you get immersed in the Italian way of life and in the city of Genova.

I would highly recommend Scuola Ttricolore, for me it was a great school offering a flexible, friendly but serious study environment.  Fantastic teacher (Laura) and all staff especially Richard willing to assist in the many issues relating to setting into the Genovese way of life.   I look forward to returning in September to continue learning the Italian language.

I studied at Scuola ABC Sestri Levante for three months over the summer. The location is beautiful, and the school overlooks Baia del Silenzio so you can go to the beach immediately after finishing classes. All the teachers are very knowledgeable, kind, and understanding. When you first arrive, the director, Monica, immediately welcomes you and gets you settled in. And by the end of your trip, if you're lucky, you might just become friends. Additionally, the school does a good job of having a variety of activities to join in the evenings and weekends so there's always something to do. The location, teachers, and Monica made studying Italian here an amazing experience and I can't wait to return. Couldn't recommend this school more! 😊

My partner and I had the most incredible experience at ABC - Scuola di lingua e cultura italiana in Sestri Levante! We took the Intensive Duetto Course, and from the moment we arrived, we felt so welcomed and supported by everyone at the school.

A huge thank you to Monica and Marina, who are truly exceptional teachers and wonderful people. Their warmth, patience, and deep knowledge of the Italian language and culture made every lesson engaging and enjoyable. They have a way of making learning fun, interactive, and incredibly effective—even when tackling tricky grammar concepts!

Beyond the classroom, the school's immersive approach allowed us to experience Italian culture firsthand. Whether through conversations, activities, or simply enjoying the stunning surroundings of Sestri Levante, we felt completely inspired and motivated to continue our Italian language journey.

If you're looking for a high-quality, welcoming, and professional Italian language school, ABC School is the perfect choice. Grazie mille, Monica and Marina, for such a memorable and enriching experience! We can't wait to return!
Excellent teachers. Nice friendly school. Highly recommended.

I went to the school in October of 2023. It is a wonderful school, with great location. Teachers are patient, kind and knowledgeable. They teach in a way that makes learning enjoyable. Monica the manager of the facility is professional and fun. She sets the marvelous atmosphere for the school. She is also a wonderful cook. Don't miss out on the student activities, such as visiting neighboring cities, cooking classes, eating together in local restaurants. On your own the school location is next to a beach, and their are ample hiking trails nearby. I highly recommend the ABC Language School in Sestri Levante.

Teachers were friendly, knowledgeable, helpful and courteous.  The school building is located on the lovely Bay of Silence.  Nice, quick and inexpensive sandwich shop (Le Delizie della Baia)  5-minute walk from the school).  Course was challenging but enjoyable.  I would do it again.  Good choice.

Before coming to Italy, I was worried about speaking Italian in front of other people. The classes at Omnilingua helped me become much more confident. The lessons were practical and focused on real communication rather than only grammar. I also liked that students of different ages could easily get along. I wish I had read a review like this before I booked my course, so I’d like to share my experience to help future students decide whether this learning style is the right fit for them.

I studied here for about three weeks.

First of all, the teachers are very kind, the staff are friendly and helpful, the school is in the city centre, and students come from many different countries. I really appreciated the international atmosphere.

The main reason for this review is simply to explain how the group classes work, because I think this is important to know before booking a long course.

The school has only two main group classes covering levels from approximately A1 to B1+. New students join every Monday. When I attended, there were around 15–20 students in one class, with students at different language levels.

Because of this, there is no fixed syllabus or fixed textbook progression. Teachers adapt each lesson according to the students who are present that day, so your learning experience can be very different from one week to the next.

Some days the lesson felt quite easy, while on other days it became much more challenging. This depended largely on the mix of students in the class rather than a fixed course progression.

As a result, it was difficult for me to build my knowledge step by step, because I never knew what would be taught the next day. This also meant I couldn’t prepare before class.

Because the classes are relatively large and students take turns answering questions and completing exercises, the pace can also be quite slow. Sometimes one exercise can take a long time because everyone participates.

Since there are only two main classes, if one class is not the right fit for your current level or learning style, the alternative class may not necessarily be a better match. Even if a class feels suitable one week, it may not feel the same the following week when new students arrive.

In my opinion, this course is not suitable for students who need a structured learning plan with predictable progress, fixed materials, and the opportunity to prepare before class.

Personally, I think this programme is better suited to students who want a one week study experience in Italy,

However, if you have a very specific goal, such as preparing for a language exam within a limited period of time, I think it is important to understand this teaching model before booking a longer course. For me, I wanted to make the best possible use of every study day, and I realised that this learning style did not match the way I learn most effectively.

If I had known this before coming, I would probably have booked one week first instead of eight weeks to see whether this teaching style suited me.

One final suggestion: once the course has started, interrupted courses are not refundable. I think it would be very helpful if this policy were made more visible on the website and during the booking process so that students can make a fully informed decision before enrolling.

1. Organizational matters: Monica, the school's head, very competently and efficiently manages the admission process and then assigns students to the appropriate group based on their Italian language level. She also selects accommodations with exceptional accuracy and in accordance with requests.

Contact before arrival at the school is practically flawless. I'm also very grateful for the accommodation offer, which I accepted: I had the pleasure of staying in a private room with a bathroom with an extremely pleasant, elegant, educated, exceptionally understanding, and friendly resident of Rimini, and the school was just a short walk away in a quiet neighborhood. It's also significant that I had the opportunity to easily park my car in a quiet part of town. Additionally, I greatly appreciate the after-class activities, especially trips to important local sites.

2. Pedagogical Issues: The classes were divided into two sections: grammar and conversation. I found this division very apt – the theoretical knowledge acquired can be immediately applied in conversations. I was fortunate to have Giulio teach both types of classes.

I must admit that I benefited greatly from his classes. He explained the grammar clearly and understandably, I'd say effectively. Then the best part came during the conversation: we were able to not only practice our newly learned grammar, but also discuss the topics that interested us most: Italian culture, sports, politics, history. Exceptionally inspiring!

I absolutely recommend it to anyone considering studying at an Italian language school!

The whole place seemed very unorganized to me, e.g. my entry exam was looked at for about 20 seconds and then I got sent to one of the only two classes possible, without any questions about why I was there or what I would want to focus on. Lessons consisted of way too much grammar in endless repetition and way too little actual speaking Italian. The material handed out was photocopies of low quality.
When we had to another teacher for a few days she had no idea what the class had done so far, apparently there had been no communication between the two teachers, so we started off to do stuff - grammar of course - that we'd already done before.
There were very little activities oranized by the school, during the three weeks they offered only two activities, everything else we had to organize on our own, like a get-together in a bar or a restaurant in the evening.
On top of all this the rooms are way to small, at times they didn't even have a place at a table for all students.

I recently attended a 1 week course. It was over 5 days with 4 hrs of lessons each day. I really enjoyed the course. The class was made up of around 5 to 6 students each day and had a good mix of ages and backgrounds, all with with similar ability levels. Our teacher Patrizia was kind and patient and made sure to involve all of the class. I feel that my Italian definately improved over the week and I would like to return in the future.

I did a 5 day course of 4 hours each morning and an extra one to one session of 1 hour on 3 afternoons that week.  The school is very friendly and the tutors very professional.  We were all encouraged to speak Italian as much as possible which was very helpful.  The teaching methods were mixed, grammar, conversation, listening exercises etc, so it was never boring.  I stayed in a cosy private apartment just 20 minutes walk from the school.  Pisa is quite small and easy to find your way around.  We had a lovely evening out with the students from other classes and the tutors and a lovely lunch on the last day with my classmates and tutors.  I would recommend the school and especially Alessio, my tutor and I would like to go back again next year to continue to improve my Italian.

I attended a 2 weeks summer course last July. I really enjoyed the class size (3 students in week 1, about 7 students in week 2) so we had enough opportunities to communicate. Also the teachers and secretary were really nice and motivated. In fact, our teacher is still in a whatsapp - group with us and still encourages us to send messages in italian even though a year has passed and he doesn`t get paid for this "extra service". To me, this shows that he likes both his job and his students :)
I would certainly recommend ILM and can´t wait to come back one day.

My favorite Italian school! Everyone is very kind and truly helps you have the most amazing experience possible. I really like the way the classes are structured; there is dedicated time for grammar and separate time for conversation, so you get the most out of both aspects. The city itself also very nice, you have everything that you need.

Top language school for Italian! The teachers are incredibly friendly and competent, and they make the lessons really engaging and practical. You can tell they are truly dedicated to their students. Highly recommended – learning here is a joy!

Last summer I attended a C1 course in Turin and was thrilled with the teaching, the school's dedication, and the free, interesting activities: 5 stars for Turin. I'd love to come back.

The two-week stay in Viareggio was less convincing, even though both teachers provided excellent instruction.

We were extremely disappointed with the "Hiking" course we booked, for which we paid 400 euros (plus a 40-euro registration fee). For this price, we were offered five walks, two of which were in Viareggio, the kind everyone takes when they arrive there. These walks lasted 1 hour and 2 minutes and 2 hours, led by an unprofessional guide, and mostly along busy roads. In the second week (costing 220 euros), we were offered two excursions on Monday and Tuesday. We felt ripped off. It's incomprehensible that a language school whose teachers do a good job would treat its students this way. A so-called "director" was only seen at this school after two weeks, on the last day; a conversation with the secretary was fruitless.

The numerous other activities, which had been grandly announced online, also failed to materialize. Even an afternoon excursion to Pisa was canceled due to a train staff strike. This could have been found online, and one could have simply taken a bus to Pisa.

I took an intensive course at this school and it was a fantastic experience. The lessons are great fun and you learn a lot. The teachers I had were very good; they proved to me that they were great teachers due to their professionalism and humanity. The activities organized were very interesting. It was undoubtedly an unforgettable experience. I highly recommend it.

What a great language experience!
I need Italian for my work so I had decided to attend a group course in the morning and two individual lessons in the afternoon with a focus on business Italian. 6 hours a day, that’s quite a lot, but honestly speaking I never had a tough time or felt tired during the lessons. The teachers were really great and the lessons very variable and interesting, so you never got bored or swamped.
Still, after the lessons I was in need of some relax and holiday feeling. It’s perfect when a language school is located so close to the beach! I took a bath in the sea or took part in some of the activities offered by the school which were a great possibility to get to know the city together with other people.
All in all, I can definitely recommend this school – a perfect combination of learning and holidays!

Il Sasso is an amazing language school. I could not recommend it enough! The class format is highly effective and helps students feel more comfortable in their language skills. My friends and family said that after three weeks they could tell a huge difference with my speaking confidence and that my comprehension improved. The school also plans excursions for its students to provide the opportunity to see other places besides Montepulciano and learn more about Italian culture. I loved all of the excursions but I think my favorite was learning how to make pasta and pici at a local pizzeria! Silvia was extremely helpful with helping me plan the details of my trip and she is even kinder in person. Alberto and Sara were amazing instructors and helped me so much with my Italian! I definitely would like to take online courses when I return home and I highly encourage anyone interested to try an online course if they are unable to travel to Montepulciano!

What a beautiful summer, experiencing the Tuscan landscape and studying Italian at Il Sasso! I was in group lessons, and afternoon private lessons for one hour. Before coming to Il Sasso, I only knew how to greet someone in Italian, and count from 1-100. Yet, by the end of one month, I have made tremendous progress and was using the A2 textbooks. This is because of my excellent teachers: Eleonora, Cinzia, Sara, Alberto and Gaia. And, if you're lucky to have Costanza as your private lesson teacher, request her! My teachers taught Italian in a living context. We were not studying just repeating grammar, but learning how to use Italian at the supermarket, and other useful situations. I highly recommend private lessons, even for just one hour, if you're really looking to improve your Italian. My success with the language is indebted to Il Sasso. Plus, Montepulciano, with all its Medieval festivities and quirks, is a memorable and unique experience. You won't regret it!

Took a three-week course at Il Sasso on a scholarship granted by the Italian Embassy. The staff were great for a first timer like myself and helped me in everything I asked for(It's that Italian culture). The class sizes were small and you could really get close to the Instructors which is great because you'd always make the effort to tell them about what adventure you were in yesterday.

P.S. I was given a little apartment on the edge of the town that had the most amazing view (coming from a city person)

Il Sasso is an amazing Italian language school! I spent three months studying at the school. During that time, I learned so much about the language and the culture. I picked up so many conversational skills while studying at Il Sasso. The teachers, staff, and faculty were impeccable. Classes were so comfortable and the teachers are so encouraging. I will most definitely return to Montepulciano to go to Il Sasso again. I feel that Montepulciano is my Italian home and Il Sasso is my Italian family. Please go to this amazing school to have the joy of learning Italian at the best language school!

We stayed seven weeks in Montepulciano, I took an intensive course at Il Sasso (group lessons in the mornings and private lessons in the afternoons) whilst my son attended  the local  kinder garden. The teaching was excellent (we were continually and constructively encouraged to speak Italian from the very beginning). My progress was good,  from complete beginner to elementary level within the first two weeks, and my son's Italian wasn't that bad either-children in his class spoke Italian only!
The teachers were thorough and helpful, as well as the school administration. The kinder garden 'maestre' were very friendly and they gave me lots of opportunities to practice the language.  Montepulciano is a small and historic town with an inclusive feel, we felt very much at home.  Our accommodation was, overall basic, however our little apartment was very near to the school, with fabulous Tuscany views. We speak Turkish and English, Italian would be an excellent addition, I do hope we can go back and continue learning this musical language.

It’s a great school; I’ve been there three times so far in the last two years, always for several weeks at a time, attending both group and one-to-one lessons. And I’ll definitely be going back. Everyone is very helpful. And there’s a friendly, family atmosphere. I like the fact that it’s a small school. The teachers go out of their way to help you, and the administration is brilliant, whether it’s shopping tips, the programme, bookings or accommodation. You always receive very warm support.

It’s a small school, and that’s exactly why it works. No hiding, no coasting. Everything is built around actually getting you to speak and improve.

Federica runs the place on the admin side and makes things easy. She’s responsive, clear, and gets things sorted fast.

The teachers are the real strength. They pay attention. They adjust. You’re not sitting through a generic lesson, rather you’re being worked with. There’s a difference.

They also run daily activities that connect you to Italian culture in a practical way. Not filler stuff - useful.

If you actually want to learn Italian, this place delivers. And doing it in Perugia helps. It’s hard to beat as a setting.

The teachers here are amazing and deserve all the respect, but the management is a nightmare. The director and her assistant are incredibly rude, unpleasant, and unprofessional. They create a disgusting atmosphere that ruins the whole experience. It’s a shame that such great teachers have to work under such toxic leadership. I strongly advise against this school as long as these two are in charge.

Terrific 2 weeks of language instruction for 2 Americans.  We arrived with a modest knowledge of conversational Italian.   We took a written and oral test and were placed into a class customized for us (roughly level A1+).  Susannah was our teacher for week one.  She masterfully created engaging lessons which featured exercises from the textbook & conversation.  Donatella was our week 2 teacher.  She is a seasoned educator and provided engaging lessons using custom exercises, flashcards, conversation.  Week 1 - Afternoons were spent with Diletta.  She lead us in walking tours of Perugia, a visit to a monastery, a visit to an olive producer, and a visit to a stained glass restorer.  Each tour was conducted in Italian and Diletta was always ready to help with understanding.   Week 2 - afternoons were spent in the kitchen at Osteria Il Gufo with chef Luca.  We prepared fresh pastas, salsa, meat dishes, fish dishes, vegetable dishes, and, of course desserts.   We have quite a bit of experience in the kitchen.  Our time with Luca expanded our cooking skills and taught us a host of local recipes.

I highly recommend this language school and its enrichment activities.   We will likely return for more classes in the future.

I just returned for more lessons. The school is small but absolutely great if you really want to learn Italian. Federica is the administrator and is super helpful. The teachers are very talented and take a real interest in helping students succeed. There are also daily activities to show you Italian culture. This is the best language school in one of the best town in Italy.

The university takes forever to release the exam results of CELI, and the staff are very rude and unfriendly, never understand why it would take almost 6months for releasing the score, it’s where you can experience the italian bureaucracy

Between my paying for the courses and applying for a study visa, the university changed the course hours so that they no longer qualify for a study visa, but they refuse to refund the money. They will do everything they can to be difficult just to be difficult and keep your money. I should have believed the other reviews here saying just that.

I really wanted to love this university. The city of Perugia is stunning — a true hidden gem — and the building itself feels like a museum. I made great friends and spoke more Italian than ever just by being immersed in the town. In that sense, my Italian has definitely improved.

Pros:
•	One of the most affordable Italian courses you can find
•	Perugia is a fantastic city for student life — safe, walkable, and filled with chances to speak Italian
•	Housing is much cheaper compared to cities like Milan or Rome, and while it may be tricky to secure from abroad, it becomes much easier to find once you’re actually in Perugia
•	You’ll meet lots of international students and practice at a similar level

Cons:
•	Very little flexibility — courses can be rigid
•	Professors are hit or miss, and student support is limited. I had two. My morning professor was awful (why I didn’t continue), my afternoon professor was nice and helpful.
•	If your Italian is below B1, it’s hard to get help in English — everything is handled in Italian
•	The course feels more exam-focused than communication-based, and there’s little emphasis on real-world speaking
•	The website frequently crashes and navigating the registration system is frustrating. Also the technology in general is limited
•	You still need to pay extra for textbooks and there are no included excursions or conversation clubs

I came from a top Italian university in the north and was already used to bureaucracy — but this was on another level. Even for someone who speaks Italian, communication and course organization were incredibly inconsistent.

It’s a shame, because I believe this university has a lot of potential. With its beautiful setting and affordability, it could be a fantastic hub for learners — especially if it offered more course variety (right now there’s only cinema and art history as extras), cultural activities, or even regular conversation groups. I’d love to see it grow into the international learning environment it has the foundation to become.
What a beautiful building. Worth visiting, both during the day and in the evening !

Building - beautiful inside and outside. Good example of renaissance palace
University - every year organization is better. Lessons? Is depend of teachers but normally level is high.

I highly recommend the Italian lessons at he Academia Lingua Italiana Assisi.  Gaia and her team have created a perfect learning environment adapted to your level.  Of course it includes the necessary classroom grammar and pronunciation lessons but it is augmented by guided excursions that will expand your understanding of Italian history and culture.  It is a wonderful learning experience.
The ALIA school is very professional, and the teachers are very competent. I spent two weeks with them and learned a lot. I recommend it without hesitation.

A fantastic school in beautiful Assisi. The teachers are excellent, the program is varied, and the school administration is incredibly flexible. I decided to take an Italian course at short notice, and within just three days, a personalized program was created for me.

I took a 2-week intensive course to refresh my Italian. Loved all the teachers, they’re very dedicated and knowledgeable. I wished I could have spent more time and Assisi and surrounding towns like Perugia are just beautiful. Great restaurants too! I highly recommend the Academy!
This is a beautiful facility with a very gracious and intelligent professors. Space is bright, perfect for learning environments.

Abbiamo trascorso due settimane fantastiche a Todi grazie alla scuola La Lingua La Vita. La scuola si trova nel cuore di questa splendida città medievale, ricca di storia, arte e atmosfera autenticamente italiana.
Gli insegnanti sono eccellenti: professionali, competenti e sempre disponibili ad aiutare gli studenti. Le lezioni sono interessanti e coinvolgenti e permettono non solo di migliorare l'italiano, ma anche di conoscere la cultura, la storia e le tradizioni dell'Umbria.
Abbiamo apprezzato molto anche il programma di attività ed escursioni organizzate dalla scuola. Le visite ad Assisi, Orvieto e alle Cascate delle Marmore sono state indimenticabili e accompagnate da guide preparate e appassionate.
Consigliamo vivamente questa scuola a chiunque desideri imparare l'italiano in un ambiente accogliente e stimolante. Studiare a Todi è stata un'esperienza meravigliosa che porteremo sempre nel cuore!
Grazie, La Lingua La Vita!

Trying to choose a language school in Italy that offers a true immersive experience? Here are 3 reasons to choose La Lingua La Vita in Todi: 1) the teachers are fabulous and focus the lessons to students’ individual levels 2) Todi is a charming medieval hilltop village that is easy to navigate on foot or by bus. There are also lots of fantastic day trips for exploring, wine tastings, truffle hunting, ceramics, cooking classes, etc 3) The townspeople are accustomed to students, so they are extremely kind and patient with us non-native speakers while we practice! It is the perfect setting to help build conversation confidence! I spent 4 lovely weeks here, which helped me prepare for the citizenship exam. Also, I have memories that will last a lifetime. Just do it!

I just finished 2 weeks of lessons at La Lingua La Vita. The school is staffed by wonderful and friendly people. A special recognition to my teacher, Martina, who patiently worked with me and helped me develop my growing Italian language skills. Todi is a wonderful city with lovely people, outstanding restaurants, a lively piazza, and a great community of artists.
This language school is very good. I learned a lot. Teaching was just in my level. Todi is a little, charming city.

I had a wonderful experience with La Lingua La Vita when I was living in Todi over the summer. From the moment Federico greeted me at the front desk, I knew I was in good hands. He was so friendly and helpful and set me up with a week long class with a group of students visiting from Philadelphia. I liked the school so much that I continued with private lessons with them through the rest of the summer. I highly recommend La Lingua La Vita!

I stayed with my friend one week in Urbania to make some progress with talking and knowing the italian language.
It was e very good experience and I enjoyed it very much. We had a warm welcome. A very nice group from all over the world and 2 wonderful teachers, who were very friendly, involved, expert and consensual with room for some humor and personal input.
We received a very good and attractive book, that makes me even more enthousiastic to learn further on this beautiful language at home.
The vouchers for diner, enoteca and musea were wonderful, the only sorrow was the fact we couldn’t follow a workshop and there was no concert of students, we hoped for.
But thanks to il direttore we could attent the XI concorso internationale di canto lyrico, with a group of Chinese singers!
Thanks for this challenging week!!

During 3 weeks in a course at Centro Studi Italiani I improved my language skills so much. The learning-material is perfectly developed. The Centro, the Teacher, the classmates, the wonderful people of Urbania, everybody was so friendly and open for someone who just began to learn Italien. I'll be back soon!

The school itself is located in a very small community, being so small they really tend to reach each student individually with their own questions and needs. The staff is so caring and nice and understanding, I went for a small program in Urbania for about 4 days and meeting the staff, and touring the city as well as the country was such an eye opening experience. If I had the choice I’d do it again!
The picture I included was our last day with our language teacher, Giacomo.

It never ceases to amaze me how diligently CSI works to make you feel at home. If you need anything, such as directions to cafes or recommendations for local restaurants, their staff will be very helpful in directing you to them. Their classes are easy and interactive to learn from. There is no problem they cannot solve, and they explain everything you need to know. The location is perfect, with local coffee shops nearby, markets, and so much more within walking distance. I was very grateful to be back and could not wait to visit CSI again next year.

I travelled to Urbania from the US for 4 weeks last month and studied at Centro Studi Italiani, and I have nothing but good things to say about this school! Based in a building from the 1600's, the atmosphere was beautiful and authentic. The location was perfect too, it was within easy walking distance to homes, cafes, grocery stores, restaurants, and the downtown area. The staff here was great, they were friendly, very accommodating, and always happy to help us. They are some of the best people I've met and I'm glad I had the opportunity to study here at Centro! I would recommend this school to anybody wanting to learn the Italian language, or to gain more knowledge in the Italian culture.

I had an incredible experience at this school!
The teachers are truly amazing — knowledgeable, patient and fun! Studying with them was enjoyable and motivating.
The school is very well organized with clear communication, smooth scheduling.
They also offer great trips, which are not only fun but also a fantastic way to learn about the Italian culture and history.
The region is beautiful and other cities are easily reachable.
I couldn’t be happier with my experience — highly recommended!

It’s an absurd ehat happened to us. A group of 22 people arrived at the airport at 7 o’clock a.m and the bus to take us to school was supposed to pick us up at 12. This fact itself is terrible but what is more disgusting is that eveybody is extremely tired from the trip and it’s 1:30 p.m but the has not come yet. This fact is to be published everywhere because it only shows total disrespect to people. This is what I feel

If you are wanting to come and study Italian in Italia this is THE PLACE.
I have been here many times over the past 7 years and have spoken to many people who have been to other schools. This school has everything.It is incredibly well run and integrates your learning with many, many field trips to experience the culture and food.
The teachers and staff are friendly and very devoted to there work.
I have made many new friends from all of the world with whom I am still in regular contact.

What a great experience. Learning Italian language, gastronomy completed with several cultural initiatives as International Dinner, Guided Tours to most important cities around, having contacts with several people from all around. A complete cross-cultural training. I certainly will take it back soon.

Scuola Dante Aligheri provides a unique Italian experience that you simply cannot find with any of the other big programs. For the month that students attend (many choose to extend their stays) the weekdays have ~4 hours of Italian class. The teachers are usually locals; many of them have taught in American universities (University of Michigan for example) and return to teach alla scuola dante aligheri in the Summer. On the weekends the teachers bring you on trips to all the major Italian cities, we visited Roma, Venezia, and Firenze (and more).

The best part of the whole trip is taking in the laid back, truly Italian lifestyle lived by the people in Castelraimondo. Most of the town's residents do not speak English (which is a break from the cities where you can never practice your Italian, everyone wants to use their English.) I highly recommend visiting in June, the weather is perfect and you will get the most out the environment and cities.

Ciao amici

P.S. Gli studente alla scuola sono diversa e bellisimma.

Centro Italiano Napoli was super flexible with my study needs in spring 2026. The administrator was very responsive to my emails. They found a teacher and a schedule that worked well for both sides. I was very appreciative and valued the experience.

I’ve had a lovely experience at Centro Italiano being taught by Amelia, Mariarosaria and Elvira. Everyone is very knowledgeable and takes their time to teach well. I’d recommend this school to others. I completed the A1 course in a month’s time.

I have had the perfect experience: Best Italian center with professional teachers who knew how to adapt the lessons according to my specific needs. A warm environment full of kindness, teamwork, empathy and passion. Cuisine, movie, museum and even pilates workshops! All of this took place in a unique and authentic city like Naples. Looking forward to coming back!

I had an amazing experience at Centro Italiano in Napoli. Each and every teacher was kind, dedicated, and focused on helping us students improve. The classes were always engaging and kept a good balance between grammar and conversational skills.
Attending the school was also a great way to meet people and practice my Italian in real life situations. Being in Napoli was absolutely fantastic, and it easy to explore this truly one of a kind city during my free time and through the culture hours offered by the school. The teachers did an incredible job of demonstrating what a unique, beautiful, and important Napoli has always been. I even learned some of the Neapolitan dialect!!
I've made many lasting friendships and feel much more confident in my Italian thanks to Centro Italiano and the wonderful teachers and staff.

I highly recommend coming to Napoli and studying Italian at Centro Italiano.  The classes are small and the teachers make it fun to learn using humor and conversation with grammar and vocabulary.  They also organize fun cultural events to enjoy the neauty and history of Naples while walking around the city or enjoying a pizza making class.   A worthwhile experience for short term and long term study of Italian language and culture

Sant'Anna is the most beautiful institution I have ever had the pleasure of attending. With its stunning waterfront location, kind faculty, and wide variety of course options, studying abroad at Sant'Anna is bound to be an unforgettable experience that you won't ever regret.

Did a study abroad in January - great institute! Good classrooms, clean organized dorms, fun classes, and located near the water with nice views. They have a nice orange and lemon garden, plus Sorrento is such a nice place to visit and easy to go to Naples or Rome. Not a big crowded city (at least not in January) and had nice, fairly warm weather for January too. They also have an app and they give you a discount card that can be used at certain places around town. I also liked that they had opportunities like cooking lessons, soccor, volunteering, etc. Very nice institute to learn - definitely recommend!

I am a tenured professor who started teaching study abroad programs more than 20 years ago. On four occasions I directed a program in Sorrento working closely with the Sant'Anna Institute. The last time was in the summer of 2022, when the highest ranking administrators in the institute treated me with more disrespect, manipulation, and incompetence than I have ever observed in a study abroad situation. I have taught these programs for 3 different universities in three different Italian cities, so I do have a solid frame of reference. While I had several troubling concerns, the main problem was that they placed us in housing owned by the most unprofessional, offensive, arrogant, and (at times) aggressively rude landlady in town. The quality of the services we received was abysmally inconsistent, even once putting the physical health and well-being of my students at risk. I will never again take a group of students to Sorrento as long as the Sant'Anna institute remains in business, and if you care about the safety and physical/mental health of your students you should do the same. My advice is to find a less expensive venue with a different third party provider. (Salerno is an excellent alternative, for example).

The University of Connecticut has enjoyed years of successful partnership with Sant’Anna institute. We are thankful to Sant’Anna Institute for their exemplary service to our students since the start of this partnership in 2014.

The opinions expressed by our faculty member that are counter to this do not represent the opinions or perspective(s) of the university. To the contrary, we have appreciated the care, quality experiences and learning our students have gained through our engagement with Sant’Anna.

Sant’Anna Institute remains one of our valued partners. We are grateful for the life transformative experiences our students have had through our partnership with this institute, and we look forward to our continued collaborations.

Office of Global Affairs,
University of Connecticut.

I just came back from my wonderful vacation in Sorrento! I stayed there two weeks studying Italian at the Sant'Anna Institute. It was a wonderful experience! Sant'Anna Institute not only offers Italian Language courses in the morning, they also organize a lot of cultural activities. I took part in a cooking class and it was amazing. The lesson took place in a cooking school in Sorrento and we learned to prepare fresh Italian pasta and pizza. The teacher was so helpful and funny.
I am completely satisfied: Sant'Anna Institute's staff and teachers are professional, helpful and always smiling; they guide the students in the discovery of Italian Culture, pushing you to immerse yourself in it.

I spent three wonderful, enriching weeks at Accademia Italiana in Salerno.  I was impressed by everyone at the school from the teachers, to the various staff members who organized cultural outings and lectures, as well as helping me with housing.  Everyone was knowledgeable, professional, welcoming, and passionate about helping me improve my Italian language skills and knowledge of the Italian culture, history and all that lovely Salerno has to offer.  Thank you to everyone at Accademia Italiana.

I loved my week at the Accademia Italiano and so wished I could stay longer. Probably two to three weeks would have been ideal. I was so impressed with the standard of teaching and knowledge of the two teachers I had (Margherita for the morning and Pina for the extra one-hour afternoon class). In addition to learning a lot, we also had a lot of fun - the other students were also great. When we stopped for morning coffee I asked others how they experienced learning in their class, and they all expressed something similar to the way we felt about ours. The private one-on-one class with Pina was just as enjoyable in a different way as I was able to go over a lot of material I had been having problems with. I just wish I could transport you guys to Australia for a while. Thanks so much for the effort you put in to make our Italian experience so rewarding.
Forgot to mention that the location of the school is very central and pleasingly just one street back from the sea, close to the ferry terminal and lots of great little restaurants and shops. Daily trips to other towns and villages were organised by the Accademia, principally to the lovely little towns along the Amalfi Coast but also to Pompeii and Salerno itself, all most enjoyable. Salerno is a lovely city, not nearly as overridden with tourists and tourists traps as, say, Amalfi, Positano and Capri. I felt absolutely at home and totally safe.

I wanted homestay accommodation because I thought it would help my Italian and I liked the idea of homecooked meals. The school organised this for me at relatively short notice and I liked the place I was assigned, except for the vertical climb each evening. I'm sure my fitness levels were boosted considerably. My landlady was very friendly, but knew how to give me space when I needed it, took pains to help me with my Italian, and she was a great cook.

It was a great experience. The school made a professional impression. They were using smart boards/screens for their lectures. The whole team is very nice and I felt welcome there. They also considered the situation that my level didn't really fit into one of their groups so they offered me individual sessions with a personal teacher. I also enjoyed very much the afternoon activities that they offer. It's very comfortable that they also offer to provide different kinds of accomodation. Finally, I think I could make some progress of my language skills even I had booked just one week.

I studied two weeks at Accademia Salerno and I think the school and the city are an excellent environment for learning Italian.
Firstly a big thank you to my teachers Dario, Rachele, and Margherita. In each week we focused on one particular grammatical concept then they built conversion/discussion around that. They use electronic “whiteboards” extensively and I thought that was useful aid to learning.
The staff are all very dedicated, each person looking after a specific function of the school and they work as a team.
The apartment the school setup for me was a 1-minute walk from the school in the historic city center.
I did several of the excursions. The highlight was the cooking class at what turned out to be the best restaurant of my visit to Italy. Overall Salerno is a real foodie town and there are excellent restaurants serving locally-sourced food. It’s possible to make your own trips in the afternoons after school to some of the towns on the Amalfi coast by boat, to the archeological sites at Pompeii and Paestum, and to Napoli.

I came to Accademia Salerno to continue to improve my knowledge of the Italian language. The staff here go above and beyond to make you feel welcome. They were always ready and willing to answer any questions or concerns.
In addition to the classes guided excursions are available. I did not personally go on any but other students enjoyed them very much.  My teacher Margherita is outstanding. She keeps a nice pace and rhythm going in the class. In addition to teaching the curriculum she allows her students to ask questions and turns them into teachable moments. She has a great sense of humor too!!  I highly recommend Accademia Italiana!

I spent a month at this school and it was a fantastic experience. I did a one week cooking class and another 3 weeks of intensive Italian. I am much more confident conversing here in Italy. Major credit given to my teacher, Erika, as well as all the staff (especially Annalisa!) for a well run academy. I hope to return next year!

This school is highly recommended if you want to learn Italian well. I had lessons from Erika Pilo. A truly top-notch teacher. I learned an incredible amount in 2 weeks. Well-structured lessons. Lots of tips. The academy is also very well organized. The support from Annalisa Reid gives a lot of confidence and helps you concentrate well on your studies. Very personal approach. The lessons are tailored to your level. There is much to experience in the surrounding area in terms of culture and nature.

I just completed a one week course at Accademia Leonardo in Salerno. It completely exceeded all of my expectations. Our instructor Erika was such a delight. Very professional, always came prepared.  Kept the class very engaging, easy to follow and fun. She always answered all of our questions.  There were only 3 of us in the class.  I had such a wonderful time and will be returning in the near future I hope.  Thank you for a wonderful experience.  Highly recommend.

I had the privilege of studying the Italian language at this school for two weeks this March, and I highly recommend it.

The teachers are amazing, providing excellent and tailored lessons for each student. They go above and beyond their duties to ensure we receive exceptional care and a fantastic experience. I wish I had more time at this school. I was able to improve my Italian significantly in a short time, thanks to their outstanding teaching! I feel incredibly fortunate to have had such great teachers here.

The office staff are also very friendly, welcoming, and always happy to assist in any way they can.

Salerno is a safe and strategically situated  town, where I was able to catch a boat almost every afternoon to visit different villages along the Amalfi Coast.

The school is within walking distance to the beach, so we often enjoyed our coffee there during breaks.

I had a marvelous time and will treasure the wonderful memories from both the school and Salerno.

Overall, this school is an amazing place to learn the language and its culture.

I am a philosophy professor specializing in Ancient Greek philosophy, and in Summer 2023 my home university paid for language study in Italy.
